FAST

Nov 9 : PNC Bank is working with cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase to let corporate and institutional clients receive payments in stablecoin, as financial firms continue to test dollar-backed cryptocurrency tokens. 
Eligible PNC clients will be able to receive payments in Circle's USDC stablecoin, which will then be automatically converted to US dollars. The companies said the service will provide businesses quicker access to funds and improve the speed of cross-border transactions, since stablecoins can be sent and received almost instantly. 
“Right now, this is about testing and learning with our clients and helping explore which of those potential features of the stablecoin are a benefit,” said Tom Lang, head of treasury management product and operations at PNC. “I think that's why we see it as such a great place to start.”
PNC last year tapped Coinbase to offer crypto trading to the bank's customers, using Coinbase's institutional "crypto-as-a-service" platform. The Pittsburgh-based financial institution also said it would offer banking services to Coinbase.

items.title: Inflación de México sube a 3,75%, más de lo esperado, y pone bajo presión el reciente recorte de tasas
items.author: Gonzalo Soto, Alex Vasquez
items.summary: La inflación general subió a 3,75% anual en octubre, por encima de las expectativas de los economistas. La medida subyacente también se aceleró, días después de que Banxico recortara su tasa de interé ...
items.body: Bloomberg — La inflación anual de México se aceleró más de lo esperado en octubre, lo que probablemente intensificará el escrutinio sobre la decisión del banco central de la semana pasada de recortar las tasas de interés ante las persistentes presiones sobre los precios. Los precios al consumidor subieron un 3,75% en octubre con respecto al año anterior, según informó el lunes el Instituto Nacional de Estadística. La cifra superó las 23 estimaciones de una encuesta de Bloomberg a economistas, cuya mediana era del 3,65%, y supuso un aumento respecto al 3,45% registrado en septiembre. Ver más: Banxico sorprende con recorte de la tasa de interés y la deja en un nivel de 6,25% La inflación subyacente, que excluye los costos volátiles de los alimentos y la energía y a la que el banco central presta especial atención, se aceleró hasta el 3,80% respecto al año anterior. Los economistas habían pronosticado un 3,78%, frente al 3,75% registrado en septiembre. Los productos y servicios que más contribuyeron al aumento de precios en octubre fueron la electricidad, que subió un 18,51%, el transporte aéreo un 26,36%, los tomates un 9,68% y el gas doméstico un 3,67%. Banxico, como se conoce al banco central, rebajó su tasa de referencia en un cuarto de punto la semana pasada en una decisión dividida, una medida que reavivó el debate sobre si los responsables de la política monetaria están relajando la política monetaria demasiado rápido antes de que la inflación haya vuelto de forma sostenible al objetivo del banco del 3%, más o menos un punto porcentual. Los cinco miembros del consejo de administración del banco central también modificaron sus orientaciones futuras, indicando que la nueva tasa probablemente se mantendría sin cambios durante un “período prolongado”. Argumentaron que mantener los costos de financiación en el nivel actual ayudaría a que la inflación convergiera hacia el objetivo, al tiempo que reconocieron que los riesgos para las perspectivas siguen inclinándose al alza. Los datos de octubre muestran que la inflación al consumidor se mantiene dentro del rango objetivo del banco central y cerca de sus pronósticos. Sin embargo, se mantiene por encima del punto medio del 3% de Banxico, con riesgos que aún se inclinan al alza. Las perturbaciones en el suministro de alimentos y el aumento de los costos de la energía están ejerciendo presión, a pesar de los subsidios gubernamentales a los combustibles, mientras que el aumento de los costos laborales y las expectativas de inflación persistentemente elevadas limitarán las caídas. Al mismo tiempo, los efectos desinflacionarios de la apreciación previa del peso y la capacidad ociosa de la economía parecen estar desvaneciéndose. Vemos un margen limitado para mayores descensos y esperamos que la inflación se mantenga cerca de los niveles actuales hasta 2027, dentro del rango objetivo, pero por encima de su punto medio y del pronóstico del 3% del banco central para el próximo año. — Felipe Hernández, economista especializado en América Latina. Ver más: Los países de América Latina donde más aumentó la deuda externa en medio de un récord global Banxico había estado considerando un recorte de un cuarto de punto a su tasa objetivo desde su decisión de política monetaria de septiembre, dado que la inflación ha estado evolucionando en línea con las proyecciones del banco, dijo la gobernadora Victoria Rodríguez Ceja en una entrevista con El Financiero publicada el lunes. Gabriela Siller, directora de análisis económico de Banco Base, afirmó que los tres miembros del consejo de administración, compuesto por cinco personas, que votaron a favor de recortar las tasas de interés la semana pasada, optaron por adoptar una postura optimista, dado que la inflación subyacente venía mostrando una tendencia a la baja durante varios meses. Además del sorpresivo recorte de un cuarto de punto, el Banco de México también mantuvo su proyección de que la inflación alcanzará su objetivo del 3% en el último trimestre de 2027. Con un tono escéptico, Siller afirmó que, “dada la reciente depreciación del peso y las presiones inflacionarias en el sector servicios, era probable que la inflación repuntara”. “No hay ninguna posibilidad de que la inflación alcance el 3% el año que viene”, dijo Siller. William Jackson, economista jefe de mercados emergentes de Capital Economics, afirmó en una nota a sus clientes que la inflación probablemente se acelerará en los próximos meses, superando la previsión del banco central del 3,7% para el último trimestre, tanto para la inflación general como para la subyacente. Ver más: ¿Qué esperan de Banxico cuatro analistas que acertaron al recorte de la tasa de interés? Lo que complica las perspectivas es la reciente reactivación de la actividad económica, ya que el producto interior bruto se expandió un 3,2% en el tercer trimestre con respecto al año anterior, el ritmo más rápido desde 2023. Banxico ha sostenido que la economía aún opera por debajo de su potencial, lo que limita la inflación impulsada por la demanda, pero una fortaleza sostenida podría dificultar la sostenibilidad de ese argumento. Rodríguez afirmó que, si bien la actividad económica ha superado recientemente las expectativas, aún existe holgura y Banxico no prevé presiones inflacionarias por el lado de la demanda. items.title: Google escalates Nvidia rivalry with specialised versions of AI chips
items.author: The Straits Times
items.summary: The roll-out marks an acceleration in product development for Google’s chip unit.
items.body:
Google escalates Nvidia rivalry with specialised versions of AI chips
Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox

Google’s latest chips will help models access a wider range of information when handling queries.
PHOTO: REUTERS

Published   Nov 09, 2026, 09:45 PM

Updated   Nov 09, 2026, 09:46 PM

Set as preferred source

Listen
Summarise

Google is widening its TPU line to challenge Nvidia, with new 8tx and 8i Max chips for secure work and long-context AI tasks.
The chips support Google’s shift towards specialised AI hardware, and the company says this brings more value, better security and lower costs for some customers.
Demand is strong, with clients like Apple, Meta, Oracle, Anthropic and Jump Trading, but Google faces supply shortages, new rivals and a possible slowdown in AI spending.

AI generated

Alphabet’s Google is rolling out a broader array of artificial intelligence chips, aiming to capitalise on its rapid ascent as a challenger to Nvidia in a market worth hundreds of billions of dollars.
The company is introducing two new variations of its tensor processing units, or TPUs, custom-made semiconductors that help develop and run AI software. The latest chips will address the need for confidential computing and help models access a wider range of information when handling queries. More broadly, they are meant to serve an industry that is shifting towards the use of AI agents and confronting security challenges. 
The roll-out marks an acceleration in product development for Google’s chip unit. The business once released a new AI processor every two years. In 2026 , it put out two at the same time. And the latest variations, due to be announced on Nov 9 , will add additional flavours to that pair of chips.

The four TPU offerings will optimise different needs, Google chip chief Amin Vahdat said in an interview. “This really follows the thesis that we have here at Google, which is that the future is going to be about specialisation, and the upsides for specialisation continue to be significant.”
Google is staking its claim at a tumultuous time for the AI chip industry. Concerns about a potential slowdown in infrastructure spending have roiled tech stocks, and US midterm elections that swept Democrats into power have raised fresh doubts about data centre projects. But the demand for AI processors from Nvidia remains larger than it can satisfy, and that has left room for Google and other contenders to build a sizeable business.
The new TPU 8tx and 8i Max variations are not completely new silicon designs – rather, they are reconfigured to take on tasks that customers have been requesting, Vahdat said.

The 8tx is aimed at handling secure, confidential work for customers like government agencies and companies in regulated industries. The system works with chips from Advanced Micro Devices, part of a collaboration between the two companies. 
The 8i Max, meanwhile, is meant to run AI applications that require long-context windows – the amount of data an AI system can consider in a single request. That is necessary for things like drug discovery and mathematics, but is also important for coding applications, Vahdat said.
TPUs compete in a market dominated by Nvidia’s graphics processing units, or GPUs. Google set out to develop the technology more than a decade ago, alongside Broadcom, which helped with design and coordinating production. The initial idea was to more efficiently handle the search giant’s burgeoning computing needs. It then realised the potential of TPUs for doing AI work and has now begun selling them outside its cloud-computing operation. 

Google’s new life as a chip seller is proving lucrative. By 2028, TPU sales will top US$135 billion (S$173 billion), including related software and hardware, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. That is up from an estimated US$12 billion in 202 6, and it does not include sales from clients using the chips through Google Cloud.
TPUs have netted some high-profile clients, including Apple, Meta Platforms and Oracle. And offering specialised versions of the chips should help Google make further progress, Vahdat said. The variations will be available in 2027 , he said.
“We could build a single chip that tries to address the whole market or, by building specialised versions of the chips, we actually can deliver much more value,” he said.
Even Nvidia, which has historically promoted its GPUs as a product for all AI tasks, is starting to offer more specialised chip systems. That includes offering its own central processing units, or CPUs, a category pioneered by Intel. Those processors do not handle the heavy-duty data crunching needed to create AI models, but they are useful for managing AI agents.
Nvidia is also offering chips more focused on the inference stage of AI – where already-trained AI models carry out tasks – using technology it acquired from start-up Groq.
Google’s 8tx pairs with a CPU from AMD, a rival to both Nvidia and Intel. The technology allows data to be encrypted at the chip level, making it more secure. Normally, the information has to be unlocked in memory while a computer processes it, Vahdat said. The 8i Max puts two TPU chips in a single package to deliver more computing power and memory. 
Part of the appeal of TPUs is their price for performance, said Mandeep Singh, an analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence. They cost about 30% less than Nvidia’s GPUs but do a competitive job in terms of throughput – the amount of data that can be processed over a given time.
The approach appeals to a variety of clients, including users in finance and other fields. Google announced during its earnings report in October that Jump Trading is a TPU customer.
That company spent several years trying out the chips before signing a larger contract with Google about a year ago, Jump Trading chief technology officer Alex Davies said in an interview.

The trading firm has thousands of TPUs, which it uses to train AI models for things like trading research. Jump still mainly uses Nvidia for training but a “vocal minority” of employees really like TPUs for their tasks, Davies said.
TPUs work very well for a subset of tasks, he said. There is a benefit to using different kinds of chips to address challenges, Davies said. “It’s actually attractive to have some problems being done differently,” he said. “You learn stuff.” 
For the areas where TPUs are as good as or better than Nvidia chips, they also offer the benefit of being more power-efficient, which lowers the cost, he said.
In October , Oracle said it had signed a deal to let its cloud customers use TPUs for the first time starting in 2027 . Oracle cloud customers previously had a choice of AI chips from Nvidia and AMD. 
“We partnered with Google because customers need more choice as AI workloads become more demanding,” Karan Batta, a senior vice-president overseeing Oracle’s cloud infrastructure, said in a statement. “This partnership expands our ability to help customers build and run AI on the infrastructure that best fits their needs.”
Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot and other services, is another TPU customer. It has an option to purchase as much as US$150 billion worth of the chips between 2028 and 2031, according to a recent regulatory filing. And OpenAI is planning to purchase TPUs as well, Bloomberg News has reported.
Google’s own status as an AI software developer has helped bolster the chip operation. TPU developers have relied on early access to Google’s latest Gemini models to improve things like power efficiency and catch bugs. That is critical in semiconductor design, where flaws can cost billions of dollars and erase months of work. AI is making those pitfalls less likely, Vahdat said.
But Google faces other challenges, including newcomers to the market. One start-up co-founded by two former TPU engineers, called Tenspresso, is focusing its first chip on long-context window inference – the same area targeted by the 8i Max. But that product is at least a year away from design completion, Bloomberg reported last week.
OpenAI and Anthropic, too, are working on in-house chip efforts – staffed with TPU veterans – providing another source of future competition. 
There is also the risk of a slowdown in AI infrastructure spending. The backlash against data centres threatens to shrink the US$1.4 trillion that technology companies were expected to spend by roughly 5% to 7% in 2027, according to Bloomberg’s Singh. That includes spending on chips, networking equipment, land and other materials for data centre construction. 
And Google’s TPU profit margins are less robust than what Nvidia generates, according to Singh.
Like the rest of the chip and AI infrastructure space, Google is also facing shortages of key components like memory and manufacturing capacity. That has made it hard to meet demand. Every TPU that Google has available is already contracted to a customer, the company said in its earnings report. 
Vahdat’s team is trying to diversify its supply sources where it can. That even means looking beyond Broadcom, which arranges manufacturing for TPUs . In recent months, Google signed a deal with Broadcom rival Marvell Technology that includes some TPU work – though the announcement was light on specifics. There have also been reports that MediaTek is doing work for Google’s TPU business. 
Vahdat declined to comment on either company’s role in the TPU business. 
William Tong, an analyst with Bloomberg Intelligence, said it is likely that Google is working out longer-term agreements “to get this supply set and prevent more bottlenecks”. BLOOMBERG

• Kumbedi plays for Wolfsburg in the German second tier.

• Kalulu has suffered a left hamstring injury, the FFF said on Monday, while Jules Kounde was not included in Zinedine Zidane's squad on Friday because of an ankle injury.

Nov 9 : Meta Platforms said on Monday it would expand its AI age-estimation technology globally to move millions more teens on Instagram into Teen Account protections, even if they have given birth dates showing they are adults, as the company faces lawsuits alleging its platforms harm young users.
Here are more details:
• Teen Accounts, available on Instagram, Facebook and Messenger, include built-in protections that automatically limit who can contact teens, the content they see and their time on the apps
• Parents in the US will begin receiving Instagram notifications this month explaining how teens are placed in age-appropriate protections, Meta said

• In Australia, Meta has begun using Apple's age-range signal as an additional method to help determine users' ages.
• Meta said it is continuing to roll out the technology on Facebook and will begin launching similar technology globally on Threads later this year
• Meta faces multiple lawsuits over allegations that its platforms harm teens
• In August, Meta struck settlements worth up to $18 billion with nearly every US state and territory to resolve lawsuits brought by attorneys general over the platforms' harm to teens
• Under the settlements, Meta agreed to improve how it identifies teens and children under 13
• Meta settled with a teen plaintiff last month in a Los Angeles trial testing claims that Instagram and Facebook were designed to be addictive, causing mental health problems and an eating disorder

BERLIN, Nov 9 : Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeness has questioned whether playmaker Jamal Musiala can ever reach top form again after being diagnosed with a neurological disorder.
Musiala, who is close to a comeback from an injury, collapsed twice in a few days in August, including six minutes after coming off the bench in Bayern's 4-2 friendly win at Heidenheim.
He was later diagnosed with a neurological disorder.
Musiala broke his leg at the Club World Cup in 2025, missing half of last season before a comeback in early 2026.

He failed to deliver for Germany at the 2026 World Cup as the four-times champions crashed out early, and has been sidelined with a hamstring injury since September.
"We are facing a dilemma in this case. He is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication," Hoeness, Bayern's influential honorary president, told Bavarian broadcaster BR. 
"But whether he will have the same performance potential that he had... Imagine if Bayern were now to question his contract and say that what he is capable of delivering now is no longer what is in the contract." 
Musiala is far from his pre-2025 best form, which included claiming the Golden Boot as joint top scorer at Euro 2024.
For Lothar Matthaeus, the former Bayern and Germany captain, Hoeness' words are his way of pushing the player.
"Uli is taking a little stab at him and he is trying to get under his skin a bit. It's part of the process not just to wrap him in cotton wool, but also to let him face a bit of adversity," Matthaeus told broadcaster Sky.
“With that statement, Uli was deliberately trying to provoke a reaction. If I were in Jamal’s position, that would be motivation enough for me to show Uli that I’m back. And that would make Uli happy."

Source: Reuters

items.title: 英ＥＶ販売、目標緩和報道は「憶測」と首相　引き続き検討中
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ロンドン ９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ロンドン ９日 ロイター] - 英政府は２０３０年の電気自動車（ＥＶ）販売比率目標を４分の１引き下げて６０％程度とすると報じられたが、バーナム首相は９日、「現時点で何も決定していない」とし、報道は「臆測」だと述べた。

首相は国内メディアで、この問題に関する意見公募で寄せられた回答を政府は引き続き検討していると表明した。

政府報道官は、ガソリンエンジンまたはディーゼルエンジンのみで走行する新車の販売を３０年に終了する方針を改めて示した。

現行制度は、自動車メーカーに年間販売台数に占めるゼロエミッション車（ＺＥＶ）の割合を段階的に引き上げることを義務付けており、２６年の目標を３３％、３０年を８０％、３５年までに１００％としている。

英紙ガーディアンは政府関係者の話として、販売比率目標を約４分の１引き下げ、６０％程度とする見通しだと報じていた。

報道官はまた、今回の販売義務制度に関する意見公募によって、３５年までに新車の乗用車とバンの販売を全てＺＥＶとする目標が変わることはないと説明した。

政府が８月に示した選択肢は、新車販売をＺＥＶに切り替えるメーカーの負担を軽減する可能性があり、既存の目標が見直しの対象となっている。

メーカーは、サプライチェーン（供給網）の混乱や消費者需要の不足から制度の要件を満たすのが困難になっていると訴えている。

英自動車工業会（ＳＭＭＴ）は先週、年初来の新車販売に占めるバッテリー式電気自動車（ＢＥＶ）の割合が２６．６％と、２６年の目標である３３％に届いていないと発表。需要に近い水準にするため、目標の「実質的な変更」を求めた。

Nov 9 : Disney and Adobe have struck a multi-year deal to co-develop custom generative AI models for the media giant with the goal of scaling AI tools across its theme parks, studio and sports media businesses.
The move, announced Monday, will start with speeding up project development timelines at Disney's Experiences division, home to its global theme parks, resorts and cruise lines, and for concept exploration at StudioLAB, the innovation hub within Walt Disney Studios.
Adobe will also work with Disney to use AI tools to boost engagement with sports fans at ESPN and bring more of ESPN's content archive to audiences.
Through Adobe's Firefly Foundry, which lets enterprises build and deploy custom AI models, the two companies will work on gen-AI models trained on Disney's intellectual properties that will generate production-ready outputs. The models will be private and proprietary to Disney.

Walt Disney Imagineering, the creative, design, and research and development arm behind Disney Experiences, has deployed a custom image generation model and a sketch-to-image model that can turn hand-drawn sketches into fully-rendered concept art.
"We talk about the time frames in our projects in years — it's years' worth of development. And what Adobe Foundry has allowed us to do is compress the creative process that would have taken months to now being able to do that in hours and days," Kyle Laughlin, senior vice president of R&D technology and engineering at Disney, said in an interview.
"We're able to run through multiple iterations quickly with these tools. And that helps us reduce costly changes in the field once we get into the construction of these experiences," Laughlin said, adding that the tools will help accelerate creative development at Disney and are "in no way meant to replace" roles at Imagineering.
Earlier this month, Bloomberg News reported that Disney was considering cutting thousands of jobs and has asked some managers to target 20 per cent in annual cost savings.

Nov 9 : Disney and Adobe have struck a multi-year deal to co-develop custom generative AI models for the media giant with the goal of scaling AI tools across its theme parks, studio and sports media businesses.
The move, announced Monday, will start with speeding up project development timelines at Disney's Experiences division, home to its global theme parks, resorts and cruise lines, and for concept exploration at StudioLAB, the innovation hub within Walt Disney Studios.
Adobe will also work with Disney to use AI tools to boost engagement with sports fans at ESPN and bring more of ESPN's content archive to audiences.
Through Adobe's Firefly Foundry, which lets enterprises build and deploy custom AI models, the two companies will work on gen-AI models trained on Disney's intellectual properties that will generate production-ready outputs. The models will be private and proprietary to Disney.

Walt Disney Imagineering, the creative, design, and research and development arm behind Disney Experiences, has deployed a custom image generation model and a sketch-to-image model that can turn hand-drawn sketches into fully-rendered concept art.
"We talk about the time frames in our projects in years — it's years' worth of development. And what Adobe Foundry has allowed us to do is compress the creative process that would have taken months to now being able to do that in hours and days," Kyle Laughlin, senior vice president of R&D technology and engineering at Disney, said in an interview.
"We're able to run through multiple iterations quickly with these tools. And that helps us reduce costly changes in the field once we get into the construction of these experiences," Laughlin said, adding that the tools will help accelerate creative development at Disney and are "in no way meant to replace" roles at Imagineering.
Earlier this month, Bloomberg News reported that Disney was considering cutting thousands of jobs and has asked some managers to target 20 per cent in annual cost savings.

Nov 9 : England fast bowler Brydon Carse, who was stood down from the national team after an incident outside a nightclub in August, has been named in the second-string England Lions squad to tour South Africa next month along with the national team.
British media reported that Carse, who has not played for England since January, may return to the senior squad for the first test, with Josh Tongue set to miss the match in Johannesburg next month for the birth of his second child.
Carse, 31, was last month charged with breaching the England and Wales Cricket Board's (ECB) professional conduct regulations over the incident in Derby. A final decision about his punishment has not yet been announced.
England have handed Nottinghamshire all-rounder Liam Patterson-White his first test call-up for the three-match series against South Africa. Batter Jacob Bethell will hope to play his first test since June after recovering from a knee injury.

Nov 9 : Alphabet's Google introduced two new variations of its in-house tensor processing units on Monday, stepping up its challenge to Nvidia's dominance in the booming market for artificial intelligence chips.
Alphabet shares were up more than 2 per cent in premarket trading. Through last close, the stock has fallen 9 per cent so far this year.
Google's TPUs have primarily been used internally for products such as Search, YouTube and Gemini, but the company has been making the chips available through its cloud business to attract enterprise AI customers.
TPU sales made a meaningful contribution to results in the September quarter, according to Alphabet, with Google Cloud revenue more than doubling to $30.71 billion.

The new chips, 8tx and 8i Max, are redesigned versions of existing processors tailored for specific customer needs, according to the company. Bloomberg News first reported the development earlier in the day.
The 8tx is aimed at government agencies and companies in regulated industries that need to keep sensitive data protected while it is being processed.
It pairs Google's chip technology with AMD's processors and encrypts data at the hardware level, delivering up to twice the speed of the previous version with virtually no trade-off in performance, the company said.
The 8i Max, meanwhile, is designed for AI applications that need to process very large amounts of information at once.
It combines two chips into a single package to provide additional memory and computing power, the company said, making it well suited for coding assistants, mathematical reasoning and drug-discovery tasks.

Source: Reuters

DUBLIN, Nov 9 : Ireland captain Dan Sheehan will miss the Nations Championship clash against Fiji on Saturday after sustaining a concussion, the Irish Rugby Football Union said on Monday.
• Hooker Sheehan was forced off before halftime in Ireland’s 42-12 win over Argentina in Dublin on Friday and will undergo a 12-day return to play protocol, leaving him a doubt for the game against South Africa on November 21.
• Sean Jansen, who won his third cap against Argentina, hurt his knee and will miss the rest of the November programme.
• Winger Rob Baloucoune (cramp) and flanker Josh van der Flier (ankle) are having their fitness monitored ahead of Saturday’s clash.

items.title: UAE Backed Colombian Mercenaries Fighting in Sudan, UN Finds
items.author: list.metadata.agency
items.summary: The United Arab Emirates helped fund and train Colombian mercenaries who fought with a Sudanese paramilitary force accused of war crimes and genocide, a recent United Nations report found.
items.body: (Bloomberg) -- The United Arab Emirates helped fund and train Colombian mercenaries who fought with a Sudanese paramilitary force accused of war crimes and genocide, a recent United Nations report found.A confidential investigation by the UN Panel of Experts on Sudan, seen by Bloomberg and shared with the UN Security Council last week, found that a UAE-based private security company recruited Colombian mercenaries to support the Rapid Support Forces. It also found that a UAE-linked base in Somalia was used to transport and train the fighters before they were deployed to Sudan.The new findings come as one of the UAE’s top diplomats, Lana Nusseibeh, vies for the role of Secretary General at the UN — a campaign that has already been criticized by the Sudan’s envoys at the world body. Sudan has been in a civil war since 2023, when a power struggle between the army and the RSF erupted into full-scale fighting, leaving tens of thousands dead and millions displaced. The conflict has become a proxy war that has drawn in regional and global powers, and the report adds to a growing body of evidence of UAE support for the RSF. The report established “conclusively” that Global Security Services Group, a UAE-based private security company, hired the mercenaries. It also found that they stopped at the UAE-linked Puntland Maritime Police Force base in Bossaso, Somalia for transit and possible training before traveling onward to Sudan.The UAE has repeatedly denied allegations about playing a role in the Sudan conflict. In a statement on Friday, the Foreign Ministry said: “UAE authorities have investigated allegations concerning GSSG” and that a UN panel of experts “has been informed of the findings.” The statement added that the “UAE has not provided arms or any kind of military support” in Sudan and has “consistently supported regional and international efforts to achieve an immediate ceasefire and protect civilians.” The UN investigation concluded that the Colombian mercenaries played a significant role in RSF military operations in Darfur, particularly in the 18-month siege and capture of the Sudanese city of El Fasher. The UN previously said there were “widespread atrocities that amount to war crimes and possible crimes against humanity” in El Fasher, with around 6,000 people were killed in just three days, the UN found. The mercenaries’ involvement included drone operation, artillery and infantry support.The report is likely to further complicate Nusseibeh’s attempt to become the top official at the UN. Her country’s role in the war in Sudan has already dogged her campaign and sparked a backlash from both human rights groups and Sudan’s government.Nusseibeh has long denied that the UAE has had anything to do with arming the RSF. When she was the UAE ambassador to the UN, she told the Security Council that allegations of UAE support for the RSF were “spurious, unfounded, and lack any credible evidence.”Since announcing her candidacy at the UN, Nusseibeh has reiterated that the war in Sudan will be a top priority for her and a “litmus test” for the success of the next secretary general.“The situation in Sudan is horrific. Ending this terrible conflict would be a priority for me as secretary general,” Nusseibeh said in a statement, adding that she has not seen the report. “Where there are findings by a UN body against any member state, I would absolutely fulfill my responsibility to act on it and engage that state,” she said.The New York Times reported earlier on the findings of the UN investigation.(Updates with UAE comment in seventh paragraph.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

Lights go out at Russia’s Novaya Gazeta, after years of defiant reporting

Reuters

MOSCOW, Nov 9 (Reuters) – Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta wound up its operations on Monday and quit its central Moscow office, bowing to what it said was a campaign of state pressure that had made it impossible to carry on reporting.

Its co-founder Dmitry Muratov, addressing journalists who gathered to witness the newspaper’s closure, issued an impassioned plea for free speech and human rights in wartime Russia.

“Those in our country who advocate for peace have been denied the right to read what they choose, as we see happening today,” he said.

Show Full Article

“We are currently at a point where the section of the Russian constitution that guarantees political and civil rights has effectively ceased to function.”

The closure marks the end of one of Russia’s most influential independent news outlets.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said it was part of a “rotational process” in a fiercely competitive media environment.

PAPER KNOWN FOR COURAGE OF REPORTERS

The newspaper, renowned for fearless reporting that led to six of its journalists being murdered over the years, was founded by Muratov and the last Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, using money from Gorbachev’s 1990 Nobel Peace Prize.

Inspired by Gorbachev’s vision of “glasnost,” or openness, it became one of Russia’s most influential newspapers and defenders of democracy, with investigations into corruption and critical coverage of politics.

After President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale war with Ukraine in 2022 and Russia imposed tight censorship laws, the paper halted its print edition but continued to publish online, becoming a refuge for independent journalists who chose to remain in the country.

But it announced late last month that it would have to close after it was designated a “foreign agent” and ordered to vacate its offices, and banks stopped processing reader donations on which it relied for financial survival.

Muratov, a co-winner of the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize, said people needed to understand that it was the Kremlin that was to blame for waging the war and suppressing free speech.

“We cannot blame the citizens themselves for this – especially the wonderful, truly remarkable younger generation. I urge you to distinguish between the Russian authorities and the Russian people,” he said.

He called for a broader ceasefire in Ukraine following a six-day truce in one area brokered by US first lady Melania Trump in late October.

Muratov also urged the release of what he said were around 4,000 political prisoners in Russia.

The Kremlin defends the need for censorship laws, denies there are any political prisoners and says that Russia is taking necessary action at a time of war to prosecute people engaged in subversive activity.

It was unclear whether the newspaper would attempt to regroup and publish in another form. In a long article on its website, describing its final weeks, journalist Irina Vorobyova was quoted as saying its spirit would survive like a “good virus”.

“Not even a nuclear explosion could destroy it. It will continue in everyone who was part of it,” she said.

(Reporting by Reuters, writing by Mark Trevelyan; Editing by Ros Russell)

ISLAMABAD, Nov 9 (Reuters) – A joint council of Saudi Arabian and Pakistani investors launched a private equity fund on Monday as part of the countries’ wider push to deepen two-way private sector trade and investment.

The Saudi-Pakistan Joint Business Council, formed by the governments of both countries, said the fund’s initial size is “multi-hundred million”, which is expected to expand based on opportunities across sectors. 

Three-fourths of the fund will be invested in Pakistan, while the rest will be invested in Saudi Arabian projects, the council said in a statement. 

Show Full Article

The launch of the fund comes at a time when Islamabad and Riyadh are deepening longstanding ties, especially in defence, amid few signs of a breakthrough in the months-long US-Iran conflict.

FAST

Nov 9 : British-Somali boxer Ramla Ali captured her first world title at the age of 37 with a split-decision victory over American Mikiah Kreps to claim the vacant WBO and IBF junior featherweight belts on Sunday in Arlington, Texas.
• Ali secured the win despite being outlanded 115-78 overall and trailing 91-70 in power punches, with Kreps landing more shots in 8 of the 10 rounds
• Ali knocked Kreps down in the third round with a right hook but was forced onto the back foot thereafter as the American responded strongly
• The judges were split, however, with two scoring the bout 97-92 and 96-93 for Ali to hand her the world titles despite the third judge scoring the bout 98-91 for Kreps
• Ali settled in London as a refugee after fleeing Somalia's civil war with her family and was the first Somali boxer to compete at the Olympic Games, representing Somalia at Tokyo 2020. She later became the first Muslim woman to win an English amateur boxing title

Source: Reuters

FAST

Nov 9 : The return of Frenkie de Jong to the Netherlands squad comes as a major boost in their quest to top their Nations League group and advance to next year’s quarter-finals, coach Xavi Hernandez said on Monday.
The injury-plagued midfielder last played for his country at this year's World Cup, missing the four Nations League fixtures in which the Dutch collected eight points to join Greece at the top of the Group A2 standings.
De Jong has long been the team's talisman and Xavi said he expected him to take a lead role again at home to Greece on Friday and away to Germany.
“He knows our philosophy, our ideas and he must be important on the pitch with us. I want to see his personality, he's one of the captains of the team, he has experience," said Xavi who coached De Jong when he was in charge at Barcelona from 2021-24.

PLAYMAKING ROLE
The 29-year-old De Jong is expected to slot back into the playmaking role where Joey Veerman impressed in two wins over Serbia and 2-2 draw in Greece.
"All the players can play together, especially the good players, and Joey is doing so well in Dortmund, and he did very well with us here," Xavi said.
"In Spain they said Iniesta and I couldn’t play together, we were too similar in our style and approach. Can you imagine?
"Frenkie will be no new discovery for me, he's a top player. He can play everywhere. Yesterday, he played as a full back for some minutes (in Barcelona’s win over Atletico Madrid). He's a top player," the coach added.
The top two teams in the group advance to the last eight in March and a win over Greece at the Johan Cruyff Arena would guarantee the Dutch a slot.
"This is the next goal, and then we will think about the other goals, but the first is to qualify to quarter-finals,” added Xavi, who took over as Netherlands coach after the World Cup.
"We showed a good level in the last window. We have confidence we will qualify.”

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

How the US was left exposed to the flesh-eating screwworm, years into the outbreak

Reuters

MEXICO CITY/WASHINGTON, Nov 9 (Reuters) – For decades, planes dropped billions of factory-bred sterile flies to keep the flesh-eating New World screwworm out of North America’s cattle. That controls the pest because sterile males mate with wild females – whose eggs then fail to hatch.

But the strategy works only if the supply of flies never runs short.

When the parasite broke through a barrier of sterile flies in Panama in early 2023, the region lacked the capacity to contain it. Efforts to scale up the fly population still lag more than three years into the outbreak, after the parasite ripped through Mexico and into the United States, according to Reuters interviews with 15 current and former officials and experts in the US, Mexico and Panama.

Show Full Article

Short on flies, the administration of US President Donald Trump closed the border with Mexico to cattle imports for more than 15 months starting in May 2025, disrupting a multibillion-dollar trade. As the border began to reopen this year, dozens of cases were confirmed in US cattle.

Mexico and Panama currently produce a total of about 150 million sterile flies a week, according to US and Mexican government data.

That’s less than a third of the 500 million per week it took during a 1960s campaign that eradicated the screwworm in the US – and that experts recommend as the benchmark to keep the pest contained to south of Panama. The US has no sterile-fly plant of its own, and one under construction in Texas isn’t expected to start production until spring 2027.

Meanwhile, the parasite has spread across most of Mexico, with about 51,000 confirmed cases. The United States has recorded 120 cases to date.

“We don’t have enough flies,” said Sonja Swiger, an entomologist at Texas A&M University. “They knew that right away.”

Efforts to make more flies at several stages of the infestation have been hampered by political transitions, funding delays, bureaucratic hurdles and rising US-Mexico tensions, current and former government officials told Reuters.

USDA spokesperson Nancy McNiff said in emailed responses to Reuters that the agency has “acted urgently and pursued every practical avenue to get more sterile flies into the field as quickly as possible.”

Spokespeople for Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico’s agriculture ministry, the Panama-United States Commission for the Eradication and Prevention of Screwworm (COPEG) and Panama’s government did not respond to requests for comment.

ALARM IN PANAMA

Screwworm larvae tear through living tissue and can kill untreated animals. A single fly can lay up to 3,000 eggs.

Releases of billions of factory-made sterile flies eradicated screwworm in the US in 1966 and contained a flare-up in Florida in 2017.

In late February 2023, officials in Panama’s Darien province confronted about 800 cases of screwworm inside the jungle that had long served as North America’s last line of defense.

Maintaining that barrier is the job of COPEG, the US-Panamanian organization that gets most of its funding from the US. In April 2023, it decided to increase sterile-fly production to 100 million a week from 20 million a week, said a Panamanian official involved in the response.

By July 2023, Panama declared the spread of screwworm an emergency, expanding sterile-fly releases, tightening livestock controls and intensifying surveillance.

In December 2023, the administration of former US President Joe Biden announced nearly $110 million in additional funding for screwworm detection and sterile-fly production in Panama and elsewhere.

In November 2024, 19 months into the expansion, Panama’s plant reached 100 million flies a week, according to the Panamanian official.

That month Mexico confirmed its first cases in Chiapas, a southern state bordering Guatemala, and began releases.

By then, the authorities knew that 100 million sterile flies a week was not enough, the Panamanian official told Reuters.

GAPS IN MEXICO

Elections in the United States and Mexico slowed the response.

In September 2024, as President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador’s administration prepared to leave office, outgoing officials warned their successors that the screwworm epidemic needed immediate attention, a Mexican official familiar with the response said.

Early planning centered on converting an existing fruit-fly plant in Metapa, Chiapas, rather than building a new plant.

The handover delayed the effort by three to four months, the official said, as the new government sorted out funding and prepared a proposal for President Claudia Sheinbaum.

In May 2025, the Trump administration announced $21 million in funding for the Metapa project. US and Mexican officials said the plant could eventually produce 60 million to 100 million sterile flies a week.

Sterile-fly drops from COPEG shifted to the Texas-Mexico border in February 2026.

Sheinbaum pushed agencies to accelerate Mexico’s plant project, seeking an April launch, according to the Mexican government official. In the end, the facility was inaugurated on June 27 – more than 18 months after the country confirmed its first screwworm case.

By then, the parasite had spread across 27 states, reaching major cattle-producing areas of Coahuila and Durango in northern Mexico, hundreds of miles from the southern border.

A PLANT IN TEXAS

The first US case was confirmed on June 3. But the US still had no production facility of its own.

USDA had begun discussing a facility in November 2024, and field staff met with Texas cattle industry groups about locations that month and in December, according to a former Biden official.

In June 2025, Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said the USDA was considering Moore Air Force Base in Edinburg, Texas, home to a retired fly plant that had been key to the success of the 1960s campaign.

This March, the Trump administration awarded a $610 million contract to M.A. Mortenson to construct the facility, according to publicly available records of the contract through a US government spending database.

The USDA initially believed the project could take up to five years, spokesperson McNiff said.

Administration officials pressed to move faster. USDA limited bids on construction, arguing that open bidding could delay a time-sensitive project, according to the spending records.

At a September meeting of the Texas A&M Board of Regents, Rollins said Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had moved the project to the top of the Army Corps’ priority list, cutting the timeline to about 18 months, or fall 2027.

John Bellinger, Rollins’ advisor on screwworm and a member of the board, said he pushed to move even faster. “For only $250 million more, we got it moved to April 1 of next year,” Bellinger told the regents, further shortening the timeline by about six months.

Mortenson spokesperson Cameron Snyder said in an email that the company is committed to working with the USDA and the Army Corps to deliver the plant quickly.

Until the plant opens, the United States remains reliant on sterile flies produced elsewhere, roughly 150 million a week combined from the plants in Panama and Metapa, Mexico.

Although Chiapas remains Mexico’s hardest-hit state, with about 8,200 confirmed infestations, USDA said all sterile flies produced in Panama and Mexico are currently being released in northern Mexico and the US.

The strategy aims to stop the parasite’s northward advance before working back south, leaving much of Mexico and Central America reliant on surveillance and treatment, rather than eradication.

Even where cases have been suppressed, protection depends on sterile flies arriving week after week, Swiger said.

Some experts estimate it could take as long as a decade to push the screwworm infestation back to Panama. That leaves North America’s defense against the pest dependent on a biological supply chain that – more than three years into the outbreak – still produces only a fraction of the needed sterile flies.

(Reporting by Cassandra Garrison and Adriana Barrera in Mexico City and Leah Douglas in Washington. Editing by Emily Schmall and Suzanne Goldenberg)

items.title: World markets bounce back after a recovery for AI stocks on Wall Street
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: World shares and U.S. futures advanced Monday after artificial intelligence stocks recovered some ground lost in last week’s sell-offs.
items.body: World shares and U.S. futures advanced Monday after artificial intelligence stocks recovered some ground lost in last week’s sell-offs. In early European trading, Germany’s DAX climbed 0.6 per cent to 25,974.42, and the CAC 40 in Paris was up 0.4 per cent, at 8,168.36. Britain’s FTSE 100 rose 0.4 per cent to 10,720.81. The future for the S&P 500 was up 0.3 per cent and that for the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.6 per cent. Taiwan’s Taiex led gains in Asia with a 4.9 per cent jump, thanks to a rebound in computer chipmaker TSMC, which surged 4.7 per cent. Regional tech stocks benefited from Friday’s rally in the U.S., where AI stocks got some relief from their sell-offs earlier in the week on worries that Democratic victories in the midterm elections could slow construction of AI data centres, particularly in Texas. Voters across political parties say they are wary about AI and don’t like increases to power bills caused by data centres. Investors also are watching to see what the Democrats’ sweeping victories will mean for markets and the broader economy. Monday trading started out strong in Tokyo, where the Nikkei 225 index closed 2.3 per cent higher at 58,775.50. Chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron climbed 2.8 per cent, giving up bigger gains earlier in the day, while Advantest, which makes testing equipment, was up 1.3 per cent. SoftBank Group’s shares fell 4.2 per cent as the company maneuvered to salvage a US$5.4 billion robotics deal with Switzerland’s ABB that Chinese regulators have rejected. In South Korea, the Kospi fell back after rising in the morning, shedding 0.8 per cent to 5,018.85. Samsung Electronics Corp. gained 0.6 per cent and chipmaker SK Hynix rose 0.4 per cent. Those are very modest gains for companies whose share prices have yo-yoed as investors dumped and then snapped up AI-related shares over the past few weeks. Elsewhere in Asia, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng edged 0.1 per cent lower to 24,448.95. The Shanghai Composite index added 0.3 per cent to 3,660.79. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 edged 0.1 per cent higher to 9,029.70. On Friday, the S&P 500 rose 0.3 per cent and trimmed its loss for the week to 2.7 per cent, which was its worst since U.S. President Donald Trump shook markets in April 2025 with his “Liberation Day” tariffs. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 0.5 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 1.1 per cent. The relative steadiness halted what had been a worldwide tumble for stocks. Indexes dropped six per cent in Tokyo and in Seoul following Wall Street’s plunge on Thursday. Friday’s biggest lift for the S&P 500 came from Nvidia, the chip company that has become the face of the boom and possible bust of the AI frenzy. Its stock climbed 2.8 per cent, coming off drops of 9.3 per cent and 3.2 per cent. Nvidia said Sunday it was opening an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. That followed Huang’s acknowledgment that he had been intimate with a business executive who, according to The New York Times, U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for China. During a routine briefing Monday, China’s Foreign Ministry dismissed the spying allegations, calling them a smear campaign against Beijing. Nvidia’s share price fell 4.1 per cent in premarket trading early Monday. Nvidia is a central player in the race to develop artificial intelligence. Its chips power many of the data centres and computing systems used to train and run AI models. Its advanced processors have also been a focus of U.S. export restrictions aimed at limiting China’s access to cutting-edge semiconductor technology. “The scrutiny surrounding Jensen Huang reaches far beyond a personal scandal, touching the increasingly sensitive intersection of U.S. technology leadership, China and national security,” Stephen Innes of SPI Asset Management said in a commentary. Despite its recent gyrations, the S&P 500 is only 5.7 per cent below its all-time high, which was set last month. A report released Friday showed U.S. employers hired many more workers last month than economists expected, in the latest signal that the U.S. economy is chugging along despite high inflation. In other dealings early Monday, Brent crude oil, the international standard, slipped two per cent to $96.38 per barrel. U.S. benchmark crude fell 1.5 per cent to $89.56 per barrel. The U.S. dollar slipped to 158.09 Japanese yen from 158.36 yen late Friday. The euro rose to $1.1188 from $1.1142. Elaine Kurtenbach, The Associated Press

items.title: El Niño podría elevar el CO₂ a niveles récord en 2027 por la menor absorción natural de carbono
items.author: Joe Wertz
items.summary: La Oficina Meteorológica del Reino Unido prevé que la concentración de dióxido de carbono aumente 3,51 partes por millón en 2027, impulsada por un fenómeno de El Niño que podría reducir la absorción n ...
items.body: Bloomberg — Según la Oficina Meteorológica del Reino Unido, un fenómeno de El Niño sin precedentes podría contribuir a provocar un aumento sin precedentes de las concentraciones de dióxido de carbono en la atmósfera el próximo año, ya que el calor y la sequía debilitan los sumideros naturales de carbono. El Niño altera los patrones de precipitaciones y puede agravar la sequía y el aumento de las temperaturas en los bosques tropicales y las turberas, lo que ralentiza el crecimiento de las plantas y la absorción de CO₂, al tiempo que aumenta la descomposición y las emisiones de carbono a través de la respiración vegetal y los incendios forestales. Esto se suma a las emisiones provocadas por el ser humano, derivadas de la quema de combustibles fósiles y la deforestación, lo que acelera la acumulación de CO₂ en la atmósfera. Ver más: Los pronósticos de El Niño para Latinoamérica entre noviembre y enero, según el CIIFEN Se prevé que esto eleve la concentración media anual de CO₂ en el Observatorio de Mauna Loa, en Hawái, en 2027 en 3,51 partes por millón con respecto al nivel estimado para este año, con un margen de error de 0,52 partes por millón, según indicó la Oficina Meteorológica en un informe. Se trataría del mayor incremento anual jamás previsto por la Oficina Meteorológica, y sería comparable al aumento récord de 3,57 partes por millón registrado en 2024, impulsado por las emisiones de los incendios forestales, según señaló. El aumento previsto de CO₂ en la atmósfera “se suma a la creciente divergencia respecto a las trayectorias compatibles con la limitación del calentamiento global a 1,5 °C", advirtió. Ver más: El Niño amenaza la oferta de banano y pone en riesgo sus bajos precios, alerta Chiquita Se prevé que el actual fenómeno de El Niño —que, según las previsiones de la Administración Nacional Oceánica y Atmosférica de Estados Unidos, alcanzará su punto álgido hacia finales de año— reduzca la absorción de carbono en la selva amazónica de Sudamérica y en los principales bosques de Centroamérica y el sudeste asiático. “Las emisiones humanas siguen impulsando el aumento a largo plazo, pero las plantas, los suelos y los océanos suelen absorber parte del CO₂ que emitimos”, afirmó por correo electrónico la científica de la Oficina Meteorológica del Reino Unido, Emily Wright. “Los fenómenos de El Niño reducen la cantidad total que absorben, lo que deja más CO₂ en la atmósfera”. NEW YORK, November 9 : The Trump administration's push to bring novel offshore perpetual futures to the US is raising alarms, according to interviews with four executives at incumbent exchanges and other key market participants who warned that the products will introduce serious new risks to the multitrillion-dollar derivatives market. 
Pioneered in non-US crypto markets, perpetual futures, or "perps," trade around the clock and do not expire, meaning investors can hold positions indefinitely. They are usually leveraged, sometimes by as much as 50 times, and are predominantly traded by retail or individual investors. 
Crypto perps trading volume reached $61.7 trillion in 2025, up 29 per cent from 2024, according to data provider CryptoQuant, with much of that on big platforms such as Binance and Hyperliquid and based in Asia. 
The Reuters interviews with executives at exchanges, trading firms, asset managers and market-structure providers revealed broader concerns that improperly regulated perps and 24-hour trading could disrupt market structure and erode risk-management safeguards bolstered after the 2007-09 financial crisis.

Traditional Wall Street exchanges were alarmed by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission's decision in May to formally approve US-listed crypto perps, with Kalshi, Coinbase, Robinhood and other financial technology firms jumping into the new market. 
Last week, the government regulator also approved single-stock equity perps. CFTC Chair Michael Selig has said it is important to maintain US oversight of the nascent market to protect American investors. 
TENSION BETWEEN ADMINISTRATION, STREET
CME Group, the big futures market operator, is suing the CFTC to overturn its May decision, arguing it has wrongly classified perps as futures, creating unfair competition and downplaying their risks. A group representing Cboe Global Markets and Citadel Securities also sued last week to reverse the CFTC's recent equity perp approval on the same grounds. 
"I think they've muddied the waters here significantly," said Terry Duffy, CME's chief executive and a 40-plus-year industry veteran. "Anytime you have ambiguity in markets ... that could hurt the business." 
The CFTC declined to comment on the concerns raised in the interviews. It has previously said the CME had chosen "lawfare" over competing in the new market. 
The clash is the latest sign that the administration's support for crypto and prediction markets, where some of the leading companies also run new exchanges, is fueling tensions with traditional Wall Street firms.
The standoff over market risks could grow next year when Democrats, propelled by midterm elections this week that handed them control of Congress, are likely to square off against President Donald Trump and step up oversight of the young industries. 
"Many of these incumbents haven't faced this type of disruption for a very long time," said Chris Perkins, head of crypto at Franklin Templeton.
EXCHANGES SAY PERPS ARE SWAPS, NOT FUTURES
The CFTC's May decision sent exchange shares tumbling on competition fears. They have since recovered and executives have said they do not view perps as a serious threat to their predominantly institutional businesses.
Their chief concern is that treating perps as futures gives retail investors access to the novel products under a regulatory regime they say provides insufficient safeguards against leverage and counterparty risk. They argue the products are more akin to swaps, which face tougher margin, capital and reporting requirements and are generally less accessible to retail investors. 
Traditional futures let counterparties lock in a transaction price for a later date, while swaps involve counterparties periodically exchanging cash flows or liabilities based on a benchmark. Because perps do not expire and involve ongoing funding payments between counterparties, they meet the 2010 Dodd-Frank Act's definition of a swap, exchanges say.
In public legal notes, derivatives attorneys have said the CME has raised legitimate issues. The CFTC has said perps have futures-like features and their funding mechanism is a substitute for expiration. 
"The industry is at an inflection point where product classification risks becoming a competitive tool," said Rob Hocking, global head of derivatives at Cboe, adding that the development is bad for markets. 
"There needs to be a resolution in short order." 
MISCLASSIFICATION, 24/7 TRADING SEEN AS RISKY
Futures-style margin requirements may be inadequate for products that behave more like swaps, increasing counterparty and liquidity risks during intense volatility, the executives said. 
Mechanisms that automatically liquidate traders' perp positions when their margin falls below required levels could amplify such stress, some said. Last year, such mechanisms triggered the biggest ever liquidation of bitcoin positions, amplifying the selloff. 
The CFTC, in an advisory to futures commission merchants, has emphasized the need for enhanced customer disclosures about auto-liquidation features during extended trading hours.
The upstart platforms, meanwhile, are pushing to extend the products into other assets. Some of their executives say that without a workable US framework, the market will continue to flourish overseas and take US investors and funds with it.
"I think it's better for those products to trade transparently inside the US regulatory perimeter than for that activity to remain offshore," said Andy Ross, Kalshi's head of institutional business. 
Some industry executives also say that perps pose market-structure risks. Because they trade continuously, the products require exchanges, clearing houses, brokers and traders to manage positions and meet margin calls around the clock.
That may work in smaller, pre-funded crypto markets, executives said, but it becomes more complex in larger markets where participants must move a lot of cash and collateral outside standard banking hours. 
The CME last month said that it had shelved its proposed 24/7 crude oil futures contract mainly because commercial clients were unwilling to staff weekend trading desks. 
"The traditional financial market infrastructure in the US is not yet fully equipped for true 24/7 markets," said Thomas Restout, chief executive of B2C2, an institutional crypto market maker.

Source: Reuters

Tech set to still sway US stock market's course despite AI-driven swoon

NEW YORK, Nov 9 : Even with the steep pullback in AI names, the US stock market is poised to rely on the performance of technology shares — and investors are on guard for obstacles that could trip up the trade in the coming weeks.
A month-long swoon in technology and AI-related stocks culminated this week in the biggest one-day drop for the S&P 500 technology sector in over six years. Investors are concerned Democratic victories in the midterm elections would lead to slower data-center spending that has been at the heart of the market's rally.
Yet even with the drop, tech remains by far the biggest sector in the S&P 500, the benchmark index for the US stock market. Although its sway has diminished modestly, the tech sector still held a greater than 35 per cent weight in the S&P 500 as of Thursday's close.
"Because so much of technology is AI-sensitive, it's going to have an impact on the entire sector, and that sector carries so much weight within the S&P 500," said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth Management. "So weakness in AI is going to drag down tech, which drags down the S&P 500."

The sector's percentage of S&P 500 market capitalization remains above the level it reached during the height of the Internet bubble era in 2000.
The tech sector alone does not fully capture AI's influence. For example, three hyperscalers spending massively on data centers — Alphabet, Amazon and Meta Platforms — are classified in other sectors.
The continued heavy weighting of technology is a byproduct of the huge gains for the sector during the US stock bull market that began in October 2022. Even with the tech sector's latest slide, it has gained more than 200 per cent over that period, nearly double the S&P 500's gain.
Some of the biggest AI winners are still logging significant year-to-date gains despite their recent slides. For example, shares of Sandisk remained up about 250 per cent in 2026, while Dell Technologies was last up about 160 per cent and Micron Technology had gained 140 per cent.
As stocks rebounded somewhat on Friday, the S&P 500 was last up nearly 8 per cent for the year, with the tech sector up about 11 per cent.
"If somebody is in a profit-taking mode, there are still profits to be had," said Chuck Carlson, CEO at Horizon Investment Services.
The slide in tech has also made valuations for the stocks appear — at least on the surface — more modest. The tech sector's forward price-to-earnings ratio — based on earnings estimates for the next 12 months — fell to 17.1 as of Thursday, according to LSEG Datastream, after it rose above 32 in October 2025.
The P/E ratio for the overall S&P 500 stood at 17.9. This week marked the first time since 2017 that the tech sector's P/E has fallen below that of the broader market.
The drop in valuations means "arguably ... the market is already pricing in a lot of bad news," said Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services.
"We are moving toward a situation where a little good news could go a long way," Lerner said in a note on Thursday.
Investors will be watching a number of potential catalysts in the coming weeks that could drive the AI trade in one direction or the other:
** ANTHROPIC IPO: Developments with the initial public offering of AI lab Anthropic are poised to drive sentiment about the AI trade. Reuters reported on Thursday that potential investors are raising doubts about whether the company can proceed with its IPO roadshow next week in time for a November listing. The discussions reflect in part the impact of the sharp tech stock swoon.
** TECH EARNINGS: While the bulk of third-quarter earnings reports have finished, some key results remain. Cloud company CoreWeave, which has been at the center of concerns about financing the AI buildout, reports on Tuesday. AI bellwether Nvidia is due on November 17, while Dell reports on November 24.
** MACRO BACKDROP: Developments involving the US-Israeli war with Iran are set to sway stocks broadly. Expectations that the shift in Congress could bring about the end to the conflict helped drive oil prices lower this week, which in turn helped stocks. But investors are wary of an escalation in tensions with the midterms finished. Investors are also closely watching the path for interest rates and how significantly the Federal Reserve will raise rates in the coming months to tamp down inflation. One test comes with next week's Consumer Price Index report.

Nov 9 : The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Monday it had opened a recall query into 2,895 vehicles operated by Alphabet's self-driving unit Waymo over continued traffic safety violations involving the vehicles' behavior when encountering school buses.
The probe will determine whether a software fix Waymo rolled out late last year failed to stop its driverless cars from passing school buses with flashing red lights, as most of the violations happened after the company said the remedy was fully deployed. 
NHTSA said it was reviewing whether a software update implemented by Waymo under a December 2025 recall adequately addressed a defect that could cause Waymo vehicles to pass school buses displaying flashing red lights or extended stop arms after initially slowing or stopping.
The auto safety regulator said most of the incidents occurred after November 2025, when Waymo said it had completed the software remedy for all affected vehicles.

The recall query will assess the adequacy of the remedy and determine the causes of the post-remedy incidents, NHTSA said.
Separately, NHTSA had opened a probe in January after one of Waymo's self-driving vehicles struck a child near an elementary school in Santa Monica, California.
In October last year, the NHTSA launched a preliminary probe into Waymo after reports emerged of robotaxis failing to obey traffic laws near school buses.
In Austin, Texas, the independent school district documented 19 distinct violations, including an incident where a driverless car briefly stopped but then proceeded while a student was actively crossing the street. Six other violations were recorded by public schools in Atlanta, Georgia.
Waymo announced a voluntary software recall in December affecting over 3,000 vehicles equipped with its fifth-generation automated driving system. The company said that the update had been fully deployed by mid-November to ensure cars appropriately slowed down and remained stationary.

LONDON, Nov 9 : McLaren Formula One driver Oscar Piastri and fellow-Australians Mark and Ann Webber have ended their management agreement, they said on Monday.
Nine-times grand prix winner Webber started working with Piastri in 2019 and was instrumental in the driver joining McLaren in 2023 in place of compatriot Daniel Ricciardo and instead of remaining with Alpine.
Renault-owned Alpine had wanted to promote Piastri to a race seat after double world champion Fernando Alonso announced he was leaving for Aston Martin, but the Australian rejected the offer. 
"We are proud to have played a pivotal role in the formative years of Oscar's career and to have placed him in F1 so that he could compete at the front so early in," Webber said in a statement.

"Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close.
"This will allow Oscar to build on his achievements under a new management structure and for us to embark on our new ventures."
Piastri, who won back to back titles in Formula Three and Formula Two in 2020 and 2021, thanked the pair for support and recognised their guidance had been invaluable.
The Australian has not won a race this season, after looking like he might win the championship last year before being overhauled by teammate Lando Norris and ending up third. He finished sixth in Brazil on Sunday.
The winner of nine grands prix has not been on the podium for 16 races and is lying seventh in this year's standings.

・電子部品輸出は６１．４％増の３２６億８０００万ドルで、月間の過去最高を更新した。

・輸入は７５．１％増の６８８億９０００万ドルと急増し、エコノミスト予想の５４．５％増を上回った。

・ＡＩの応用、高性能コンピューティング、クラウドサービスは引き続き拡大した。

items.title: Lights to go out at Russia's Novaya Gazeta, independent newspaper known for its fearless reporting
items.author: CNA
items.summary: The newspaper announced last month that it would have to close after it was designated a "foreign agent".
items.body:

World

Lights to go out at Russia's Novaya Gazeta, independent newspaper known for its fearless reporting

The newspaper announced last month that it would have to close after it was designated a "foreign agent". 

The Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta edition with a portrait of slain investigative journalist Anna Politkovskaya lies in the outlet's office as the newspaper shuts down, citing what it describes as a relentless campaign by the authorities, in Moscow, Russia, Nov 9, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Ramil Sitdikov)

FAST

MOSCOW: Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta was winding up its operations on Monday (Nov 9) and preparing to quit its central Moscow office after holding its final editorial meeting, bowing to what it said was a campaign of state pressure that had made it impossible to carry on reporting.
The paper, founded by the last Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev with money from his 1990 Nobel Peace Prize, had kept going until now despite a sharp tightening of censorship after Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in 2022.
But it announced late last month that it would have to close after it was designated a "foreign agent" and banks stopped processing reader donations on which it relied for its financial survival. Its offices and the home of its editor were searched, and another senior journalist is under house arrest awaiting trial.
"The most awful thing is that we who lead editorial teams cannot protect our journalists," former editor in chief Dmitry Muratov told an audience in London last month.

Muratov shared the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize, dedicating it to six slain colleagues, including investigative journalist Anna Politkovskaya, who wrote about Russia's wars in the restive Chechnya region.

Employees pack up at the office of Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta after the outlet announced plans to shut down, citing what it described as a relentless campaign by the authorities, in Moscow, Russia, on Oct 30, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Yulia Morozova)

The Kremlin - which accuses foreign intelligence services of trying to stir discontent in Russian society - has said previously that some censorship is necessary at a time when Russia is locked in what it calls an existential struggle with the West over Ukraine and some hardliner war bloggers have accused Novaya Gazeta of systematically promoting an anti-Russian narrative, an allegation it has repeatedly dismissed as false. 
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov played down the outlet's closure on Monday, saying it was part of what he called "a standard rotational process" in which some media closed only to have their places taken by newcomers in what he said was a fiercely competitive media environment.    
A long article on Novaya Gazeta's website described its journalists' operation to pack up and vacate their premises. It quoted a senior journalist, Irina Vorobyova, as saying its spirit would survive like a "good virus" - "Not even a nuclear explosion could destroy it. It will continue in everyone who was part of it."

Source: Reuters/lk

items.title: China extends suspension of new rare earth controls until January 10
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: Beijing extended the suspension of export controls on certain rare earths, industrial diamonds and lithium battery technology as it negotiates a broader trade deal with Washington ...
items.body: China on Monday announced a two-month extension of export-control waivers due to expire this month, preserving part of a wide-ranging deal struck after a summit between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump. China introduced export controls on certain rare earths in April 2025, only to expand them further in October of that year, dramatically widening their scope and also adding new controls on certain diamonds with industrial applications and lithium battery technology. The measures were then paused for one year last November after a summit in South Korea between Xi and Trump. The Ministry of Commerce said in a short statement on Monday that the pause would be extended for two months until January 10. It gave no other details. The extension is part of a broader suspension of trade countermeasures and tariffs announced by China on Monday as it negotiates with Washington over an enduring trade deal. Trump is set to travel to Shenzhen in southern China later this month for an APEC leaders summit, where he is expected to meet with Xi.

Iran defends two-day proposal for peace talks after US rejects conditions

Iran defended a proposal on Monday (Nov 9) to restart peace talks in as few as two days, after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called some conditions "outrageous and ridiculous".

DUBAI: Iran defended a proposal on Monday (Nov 9) to restart peace talks in as few as two days as the most reasonable offer on the table, after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called some of Iran's conditions "outrageous and ridiculous".
"Is it unreasonable that Iran demands that US illegal sanctions and its naval blockade must be lifted before negotiations start and that the war should end on all fronts?" Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told a weekly press conference in response to Rubio's remarks.
Iran has made the offer to shorten the time to restart talks from an earlier seven-day proposal, which calls for Washington to first meet conditions including halting hostilities, lifting a blockade and waiving sanctions.
Baghaei also said US pressure on Iraq to close most of its borders with Iran should not affect bilateral ties with Baghdad, after Iraq's foreign minister said Washington was pushing for such a move.
Baghaei dismissed a US military task force aimed at restricting Iran's land trade as a diversion following President Donald Trump 's Republicans' losses in midterm elections.

Source: Reuters/ht

items.body:

[東京 ９日 ロイター] - ＡＩ（人工知能）開発を手掛けるサカナＡＩ（東京都港区）が新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）に向けた準備を進めていることが９日、分かった。関係者が明らかにした。メルカリが２０１８年にＩＰＯした際の初値ベースの時価総額約６７６０億円を超える国内最大級のＩＰＯとなる可能性がある。

順調に進めば来年秋か来年中に実施する可能性も視野に入るという。日米同時でのＩＰＯも排除していない。

米金融大手ゴールドマン・サックスなどをアドバイザーとしている。関係者は、グローバルな今後の事業展開を考えれば、ナスダックで上場することが望ましいとの考えもある、としている。

同社広報は「ＩＰＯについて、何ら正式決定が行われたとの事実はない」とし、「引き続き、世界最先端の技術開発と、日本でのＡＩの社会実装に邁進していく」とコメントするにとどめた。

サカナＡＩの上場準備については、日経新聞電子版が９日、最初に報じた。

・センティックス指数は２．４で、１０月の２．７から低下。アナリスト予想は２．１だった。

・調査は１１月５─７日、機関投資家２２０人を含む投資家１０２５人を対象に実施した。

・一方、ドイツ経済には安定化の兆しが見られ、指数は０．３ポイント上昇してマイナス３．３となった。

・調査は１１月５─７日、機関投資家２２０人を含む投資家１０２５人を対象に実施した。

items.title: This Is How New York City Takes Out Its Trash
items.summary: According to Joshua Goodman, trash collection in New York is one of the last services the city offers that is not yet touched by neoliberalism. What he means is that it's the last free and unlimited city service — there is no opt-in; it is not means tested. Goodman — who is the DSNY's deputy commissioner for public affairs and customer experience — tells us that the city deals with 24 million pounds of trash every day, and on today's podcast, he explains the logistical dance required to sort through all that garbage. We also get into why NYC produces less trash than you might think, the DSNY's new containerization program (and the new side-loading trucks they built in less than 18 months), and why recycling is not a scam. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: 中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝中国上昇、当局の安定化支援を好感　香港小幅下落
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [上海 ９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[上海 ９日 ロイター] - 中国株式市場は上昇して引けた。アジアの他市場の株高に追随したほか、中国政府が市場安定に向けた取り組み強化を打ち出したことが支援材料となった。一方、香港株は小幅に下落した。

上海総合指数は０．３％高、ＣＳＩ３００指数は０．１％高で終了した。

深セン総合指数は横ばい。深セン証券取引所の新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は０．３％下落した一方、上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け市場「科創板」５０指数は０．３％上昇した。

中国国営中央テレビ（ＣＣＴＶ）によると、国務院（内閣に相当）は６日、資本市場を安定させる仕組みを改善し、株式市場自体の安定性を高める方針を表明した。

ソシエテ・ジェネラルのアナリストはリポートで「中国の経済指標と株価動向が再び政策当局の許容限度を超えるほど悪化し、新たな株式市場支援策を促した」と指摘。「こうした措置は投資家心理の下支えとなる可能性があるが、持続的な株価上昇には企業利益の拡大が必要で、そのためには内需の改善と物価の持ち直しが求められる」とし、より強力な財政支援がなければ、依然として実現は難しいと述べた。

９日発表の統計によると、１０月の生産者物価指数（ＰＰＩ）の上昇率は約４年半ぶりの高水準となった。世界的な原油高が製造コストを押し上げた。一方、内需の弱さを背景に消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）の伸びは鈍化した。

ロイター調査によると、１０月の中国財輸出は３割以上増加したと見込まれている。内需の弱さを補う支援材料となる一方、年初来の貿易黒字が１兆ドルを超え、貿易相手国の反発を一段と強める恐れがある。

香港市場では、ハンセン指数が０．１％下落し、ハンセンテック指数は０．９％下落した。

中国は９日、米国からの輸入品に対する２４％の追加関税と、米国関連船舶への特別港湾使用料について、適用停止を２カ月延長すると発表した。

items.title: ニトリＨＤ、不正アクセスで最大3762万件の個人情報流出の可能性
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [東京 ９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[東京 ９日 ロイター] - ニトリホールディングスは９日、同社が管理するシステムへの第三者による不正アクセスにより、最大３７６２万件の個人情報が外部に流出した可能性があると発表した。不正アクセスは６日に判明し、同日中に当該アクセスを遮断した。クレジットカード情報やログインパスワードは含まれていない。

流出した可能性のある情報は、会員番号、氏名、メールアドレス、住所、電話番号、生年月日、性別のほか、法人会員の会社名、担当者情報、注文データ。

１０月中旬から下旬にかけても第三者によるアクセスが行われた可能性が確認されており、詳細は引き続き調査中としている。現時点では連結業績への影響は限定的と見込んでいる。

items.body:
［９日　ロイター］ - ドイツ連邦統計庁が９日発表した９月の輸出は前月比２％増加で、市場予想を上回った。主に欧州連合（ＥＵ）諸国からの需要が押し上げた。

ロイターがまとめたアナリスト予想は０．５％増だった。７月と８月は２カ月連続で減少していた。

ベートマンＨＡＬ銀行のチーフエコノミスト、アレクサンダー・クリューガー氏は、今回の統計はドイツ経済全体にとって良い兆候であり、中国との競争に対する一定の底堅さを示していると指摘。「貿易は当面、経済成長を下支えする可能性が高い。ただ牽引（けんいん）役とはならないだろう」と述べた。

輸入は前月比４．２％増となり、予想の０．５％増を大きく上回った。
