items.title: 焦点：バンス氏、次期大統領選に向け戦略再構築　トランプ氏との距離感が課題
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Jacob Bogage

[ワシントン ７日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Jacob Bogage

[ワシントン ７日 ロイター] - 米中間選挙の終盤、共和党の退潮を食い止めようと、バンス副大統領（４２）は戦略を転換した。トランプ大統領についての言及を減らし、自らの政治姿勢を特徴付ける政策課題について、より多く語り始めた。

中間選挙に向けた９月の共和党大会以降にバンス氏が行った６回の演説をロイターが検証したところ、ほぼ全てが自らが掲げる政策を軸に、共和党への支持を訴える内容だった。

世論調査が、トランプ氏の支持率低迷が共和党候補者らの足を引っ張っていることを示していた中で、バンス氏はイラン戦争や強制送還といったトランプ氏の代名詞的な政策への言及を避けた。

バンス氏の戦略に詳しい関係者２人によると、この変更は意図的なものだった。バンス氏と側近らは、同氏が主張してきた経済ナショナリズム、抑制的な外交政策、治安維持を、同氏が説得力を持って語れる、政治的な訴求力の強いテーマだと考えていた。トランプ氏がこれらを「ＭＡＧＡ（米国を再び偉大に）」運動の一部として受け入れる一方で、バンス氏はその主導的な論客に浮上していたと、関係者は言う。

この戦略転換からは、共和党の大統領候補指名争いに向けてバンス氏がどのように独自の道を切り開いていくかが垣間見える。

バンス氏は２０２８年の大統領選に出馬するかどうかを表明しておらず、トランプ氏も同氏を含め誰も推薦していない。しかしバンス氏は有力候補と見なされており、一部の共和党幹部は、同氏はトランプ氏の支持基盤の多くを継承しつつも、その負の遺産と一線を画す必要があると語る。

バンス氏は４日、異例なほど率直な選挙総括を行い、自身の政治的ブランドを強化するための一歩を踏み出した。同氏は交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）への投稿で、共和党惨敗の原因として対イラン戦争を挙げ、党勢立て直しに向けた基本方針を示した。

紛争の迅速な終結を呼びかけ、共和党は物価高や生活費の問題に注力し、外交関係を再評価し、米国とイスラエルとの関係も見直すべきだと訴えた。

＜戦争終結を公然と支持＞

この投稿によって、バンス氏は初めて公然と戦争終結を支持した。

ホワイトハウスとバンス氏の広報に詳しい関係者３人がロイターに語ったところでは、バンス氏はトランプ氏と決裂してはおらず、ホワイトハウスのワイルズ首席補佐官はバンス氏の投稿を事前に把握していた。

トランプ氏が事前に投稿を把握していたかについて、ロイターは確認できなかった。

大統領の長男であるドナルド・トランプ・ジュニア氏は、一部の保守派仲間とともに、ＳＮＳ上でバンス氏の主張を支持した。

共和党の参謀マイケル・リッチ氏は、このやりとりがトランプ氏後の保守派代表としてのバンス氏の存在感をさらに高めたと言う。

＜副大統領というメガホン＞

リッチ氏によると、バンス氏のメッセージによって保守派は、戦争の是非、さらには２８年の共和党大統領候補が受け入れるべき核心的原則について議論せざるを得なくなった。

「バンス氏がトランプ氏との差別化を図っている、という見方は単純過ぎる。これは、彼が副大統領というメガホンを利用して議論の土台を設定しているという話なのだ」という。

バンス氏の代表者はコメントを控えた。

民主党側は、２８年大統領選でバンス氏を含む共和党候補をトランプ氏と結びつける構えで、トランプ氏が候補者選びに大きく関与すれば、民主党は両者の結び付きを一段と強調するとみられる。

民主党の参謀イゴール・ボルスキー氏は「（トランプ氏に）忠誠を見せながら予備選で勝利し、本選で勝てる候補としていかに自らを位置づけるかが大きな課題となる」と語る。

中間選挙でバンス氏のブランドが傷つかなかったわけではない。同氏が応援演説を行った州で共和党は敗北した。また同氏が支持した選挙戦略の幾つかは、共和党に不利に働いた可能性がある。

他の潜在的な大統領選候補者たちも、中間選挙の敗北に関する独自の分析を示している。テキサス州選出のテッド・クルーズ上院議員は、共和党が生活費の問題に対して十分な取り組みを行わなかったと述べた。フロリダ州のデサンティス知事は、敗北した候補者らがトランスジェンダーの問題に過剰に集中し、データセンターや人工知能（ＡＩ）を巡る有権者の懸念を軽視したと述べた。ルビオ国務長官は沈黙を守っている。

議論の方向性を形作ろうとするバンス氏の取り組みは、選挙戦の終盤に顕著だった。

演説で同氏は有権者に対し、共和党が連邦の医療費や貧困対策プログラムにおける不正を調査し、移民や生活費対策に関連付けていくと訴え、党への支持を呼びかけた。対イラン戦争やガソリン価格には一切と言っていいほど触れず、トランプ氏の名も滅多に口にしなかった。

ノースカロライナ州の集会では「私は自分の子供たちが、活気に満ち、繁栄し、自由で豊かな国で家族を育てることを望んでいる。望むのはシンプルな事だ。自分自身のためにそれを望むからこそ、皆様のためにも望むのだ」と訴えた。

items.title: アンソロピック、発電機確保へ34億ドル契約　データセンター向け＝ＦＴ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［８日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［８日　ロイター］ - 人工知能（ＡＩ）新興企業アンソロピックが、データセンター向けのガス火力発電機を確保するため、約３４億ドルの契約を結んだ。英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）が８日報じた。

報道によると、アンソロピックは９月下旬、米テキサス州サンアントニオに拠点を置く機器供給会社ＯｎｅＰＷＲソリューションズから、総出力１．７ギガワットの大型発電機の供給を受ける権利を購入した。

ＦＴが事情に詳しい関係者の話として報じたところによると、アンソロピックはＯｎｅＰＷＲ自体を買収したわけではなく、従業員の移籍もなかった。ただ、契約には発電機の設置に必要なエンジニアリング・建設の能力も含まれていたという。

ロイターは報道内容を直ちに確認できなかった。アンソロピックとＯｎｅＰＷＲはコメント要請に回答しなかった。

アンソロピックはＡＩモデル「クロード」への旺盛な需要を受け、計算能力と電力供給能力の追加確保を進めている。ロイターは９月、同社が今後１０年間でＡＩインフラ構築に５０００億ドル超を支出する見通しだと報じた。

items.title: イケア、通期決算は減収減益　売上高は3年連続減少
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Helen Reid

[ロンドン ６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Helen Reid

[ロンドン ６日 ロイター] - スウェーデン家具大手イケアの世界全体のフランチャイズとブランドを管理する持ち株会社インター・イケアが６日発表した２０２６年度（２０２５年９月ー２６年８月）通期決算は、売上高が３年連続の減少となった。中東紛争に起因するコスト上昇に加え、価格引き下げ策を講じたにもかかわらず節約志向の消費者からの需要が低迷していることを背景に、苦戦が続いている。

売上高は前年比２％減の４３８億ユーロ（４９０億ドル）となった。純利益は１４億ユーロで、前年の１５億ユーロから減少した。

今年初めに最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）に就任したヤクブ・ヤンコフスキ氏は「売上高はここ数年伸び悩んでおり、より多くの人々に手頃な価格の家具を提供するためには、再び成長軌道に戻る必要がある」と述べ、より多くの製品を販売し、生活費の高騰に苦しむ家庭により手頃な価格で商品を提供することが目標だと強調した。

同社は消費者需要の低迷が購入量の減少を招いたほか、サプライヤーと自社製造拠点において生産能力を効率的に活用できない状況をもたらしたと説明。また中東紛争によるエネルギー価格の高騰に伴い、運賃上昇にも直面している。

イケアは郊外にある巨大な青い大型店舗で知られているが、最近では車を使わなくても気軽に立ち寄って商品を購入できる都心部の小規模店舗の展開に重点を移している。

２０２６年度に欧州で１５店舗の小規模店舗を開設したが、消費者需要が振るわない中国では７店舗を閉鎖した。また５月にはコスト削減を図るため、従業員を８５０人削減した。

items.title: From Nvidia to Micron: Major China-linked espionage cases under scrutiny
items.summary: From Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to Micron's semiconductor trade secrets, explore major cases of alleged Chinese honeytrapping, political influence and corporate espionage.
items.body:
Home / World News / From Nvidia to Micron: Major China-linked espionage cases under scrutiny

From Nvidia to Micron: Major China-linked espionage cases under scrutiny Nvidia's probe into alleged Chinese intelligence targeting of CEO Jensen Huang puts the spotlight on past cases involving honeytrapping, political influence, trade secret theft and cyber espionage

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's case has brought renewed attention to concerns over corporate espionage and intelligence gathering. | Image: Bloomberg

Sarjna Rai New Delhi 5 min read Last Updated : Nov 09 2026 | 5:16 PM IST

Listen to This Article

  Nvidia is investigating whether its Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence through a personal relationship, bringing renewed attention to allegations of honeytrapping and corporate espionage.
  According to The New York Times , United States (US) intelligence suspects that Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed, was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to cultivate a relationship with Huang and gather information about him. Meanwhile, Megaspeed has come under scrutiny over allegations that it helped Chinese entities access Nvidia AI chips restricted under US export controls. Huang has also acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family and colleagues.
 

  China has rejected the allegations, with Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun calling the claims of a Chinese spy plot against Huang "unsubstantiated" and a smear campaign against Beijing.
  The allegations come amid intensifying competition between the US and China over artificial intelligence and semiconductor technology, where access to sensitive information and influential business networks can offer a significant strategic advantage.
  What is honeytrapping?   Honeytrapping is an intelligence-gathering technique in which an individual uses romantic or intimate relationships to gain access to confidential information, influence decisions or compromise a target.
Also Read

The G2 illusion

Got your first Diwali bonus? 5 smart ways to save, invest and spend

Saudi Arabia tightens hiring rules: Saudization salary bar to rise by 2028

How a hedge fund's warning against Nvidia gained relevance six months later

China extends suspension of new rare earth controls until January 10

  The person being targeted may be a government official, corporate executive, scientist or employee with access to sensitive information. Rather than relying on conventional surveillance, the operation uses emotional attachment, trust or the possibility of blackmail to achieve its objectives.

  However, honeytrapping does not always involve stealing classified documents. It can also involve cultivating an influential relationship to shape business decisions, secure introductions or gain access to important networks.
  While the Nvidia allegations have brought honeytrapping back into the spotlight, several other cases illustrate the different methods used to obtain sensitive information or cultivate political influence. Not all these cases involved proven honeytrapping operations.
  Major China-linked honeytrapping and influence cases
  1. Christine Fang, a Chinese national suspected by US intelligence of working for China's Ministry of State Security, allegedly cultivated relationships with American politicians to gain access to influential political circles.
  According to an investigation by Axios , she built connections with local and national politicians through fundraising, networking and personal relationships. She reportedly had romantic relationships with at least two Midwestern mayors and developed links with then-Congressman Eric Swalwell.

  The FBI reportedly alerted Swalwell to its concerns in 2015, after which he cut off contact with Fang.
  2. Benjamin Bishop, a former US Army lieutenant colonel and civilian defence contractor at US Pacific Command, was sentenced to 87 months in prison in September 2014 for sharing classified military information allegedly with a 27-year-old Chinese woman with whom he was romantically involved.
  The two reportedly met at a military-related conference in Hawaii. Bishop emailed her classified information concerning US military planning and joint operations with South Korea. He also removed classified documents from his workplace.
  Bishop pleaded guilty to communicating classified national defence information to an unauthorised person and unlawfully retaining classified documents.

  3. Another prominent case involving personal relationships dates back to 2003, when the FBI arrested Katrina Leung, a Chinese-American businesswoman accused of passing classified information to China.
  According to the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), Leung had persuaded an FBI agent to share classified information with her over a period of 10 years, which she then passed to China. The case illustrated how personal relationships could be exploited to obtain sensitive intelligence.
  4. A 2024 Financial Times report highlighted questions raised by French lawmakers over marriages between Chinese female students and sailors stationed at French naval bases in Brest. The relationships prompted concerns about possible intelligence-gathering activities, although they were not established as honeytrap operations.

  As competition between countries increasingly extends to technology and commercial capabilities, companies have become targets for attempts to obtain proprietary research, trade secrets and technological expertise. Such activities fall under the broader practice of corporate espionage.
  What is corporate espionage?   Corporate espionage involves the covert or illegal acquisition of confidential business information, intellectual property, trade secrets or technological expertise to gain a competitive or strategic advantage.
  Unlike conventional industrial competition, it involves methods such as hacking, insider recruitment, employee poaching and unauthorised access to proprietary research.
  Some notable cases with Chinese-links include:
  1. In 2018, the US Department of Justice charged Chinese state-owned semiconductor company Fujian Jinhua, Taiwan-based United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) and three individuals with conspiring to steal trade secrets from US chipmaker Micron Technology.

  The former Micron employees downloaded confidential files containing information about the design and manufacture of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips before moving to UMC. One employee reportedly downloaded more than 900 confidential files.
  The alleged objective was to transfer Micron's technology to Jinhua, helping it develop advanced memory chips without years of independent research and development.
  2. In May 2022, cybersecurity firm Cybereason reported that a Chinese state-linked hacking group, identified as APT41, had conducted a prolonged cyber espionage campaign against around 30 multinational companies.
  Dubbed Operation CuckooBees, the campaign allegedly targeted businesses in the manufacturing, energy and pharmaceutical sectors across North America, Europe and Asia.

  According to CBS News report, the hackers stole hundreds of gigabytes of sensitive information, including engineering blueprints, manufacturing designs, pharmaceutical research and proprietary formulas. The estimated value of the intellectual property stolen ran into trillions of dollars.
  The scale of Chinese espionage is also reflected in a survey by the CSIS, which identified 224 publicly reported incidents targeting US since 2000. Of these, 54 per cent sought commercial technologies, while 46 per cent involved cyber espionage. The survey also highlighted the continued use of traditional recruitment methods, including intimate relationships and financial incentives, to obtain sensitive information.

FAST

ANTALYA, Türkiye: Representatives from nearly 200 countries will gather on Türkiye's Mediterranean coast on Monday (Nov 9) for two weeks of climate talks, as war-driven energy security fears, surging AI power demand and US disengagement put new pressure on the fight against global warming.
The US war with Iran has nations scrambling for oil cargoes and firing up coal plants ; the rapid rollout of AI is pumping up power demand; and the world’s top historic greenhouse gas emitter is shunning climate cooperation for the second year running.
All that has created a challenging backdrop destined to complicate efforts by COP31 host Türkiye to land a strong deal, according to observers. "It's hard to be optimistic," said John Holdren, a professor of environmental policy at Harvard University.
Türkiye's COP31 presidency has centered this year's UN-sponsored summit on a goal to electrify more than a third of the global economy by 2035, up from around a fifth today. It is asking nations to sign onto a pledge supporting that target.

Theoretically, such a goal could help reduce planet-warming emissions by speeding the global shift away from fossil fuel-powered vehicles, furnaces, boilers, cookstoves, and other greenhouse gas-emitting equipment.
But climate advocates have criticised the pledge because it does not require that the additional electricity come from low-carbon sources. This has set up an early fight over whether electrification alone should count as climate progress.
A coalition of countries, including South Pacific island nations most vulnerable to sea level rise, are pushing more generally for a clearer global roadmap away from fossil fuels – a perennially controversial topic at climate summits.
Many oil- and gas-producing nations, including Saudi Arabia, argue that fossil fuels can still form a substantial part of the global energy mix in a climate-friendly world, provided they are paired with technologies that reduce or capture emissions.
Pressure is mounting for faster action on climate change.
A report by the United Nations Environment Programme published in October said the world is already set to overshoot 1.5°C of warming above pre-industrial times, the threshold set at the 2015 Paris climate summit.

Related:

Climate talks will be tougher at COP31 amid heightened global tensions: Grace Fu

World's climate pledges would cut emissions a tenth of what's needed: UN

2026 also stood out with a series of extreme heatwaves across Western Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that caused a catastrophic flood that killed more than 1,450 people , with thousands still missing.
"This year has proven to be one of the years with the highest casualties by the climate-induced disasters," said Manjeet Dal, an adviser to the Least Developed Country bloc and south Asia director of Climate Analytics.
WAR AND TECH The Iran war has underscored the world's attachment to fossil fuels, as has Russia's invasion of Ukraine and the ensuing sanctions on Moscow's energy exports. Some say disruptions from the wars have also clarified the benefits of turning to renewables.
The Iran war, now in its ninth month, severely disrupted Middle East oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, lifting fuel prices around the globe and leading governments to scramble for new supplies.
US President Donald Trump's administration has encouraged policies maximizing oil, gas, and coal production to address the Mideast disruptions. South Korea, India, Thailand and other Asian nations, meanwhile, have increased their reliance on coal or taken steps to boost coal-fired power generation.
"A lot of people who previously might have been embarrassed to argue for continuing very high use of fossil fuel are now feeling empowered to make that case," said Holdren of Harvard.

Related:

UN General Assembly: Wars, geopolitical divides, AI and climate change test global cooperation

Commentary: Fossil fuels are winning the battle for easy money

At the same time, the deployment of renewable energy has also risen, driven by surging exports of cheap clean tech from China, cheering advocates for ambitious climate action.
"The war has strengthened the case for accelerating the energy transition. The United States is something of an outlier in this regard," said Andre Correa do Lago, a Brazilian diplomat who presided over last year’s COP.
AI has also added a wrinkle. The technology's rapid rollout is driving a surge in global power demand, contributing to rising greenhouse gas emissions. But its benefits are proving irresistible, even to climate and environment activist groups.
COP31 host Türkiye will call on governments, businesses and other institutions at the conference to sign a pledge outlining principles to ensure AI is developed and deployed sustainably.
Business advocates said they want just one thing from COP31: Clarity.
"Delivery cannot remain a slogan or be left to voluntary initiatives," said John Denton, the secretary general of the International Chamber of Commerce. "COP31 must send clear policy signals that give businesses the confidence to invest in electrification and the wider energy transition — and turn adaptation needs into bankable projects."

Source: Reuters/lk

ＮＴＴや三菱電、三菱ＵＦＪ銀など5社、衛星コンステレーション事業化へ協業
12:30 配信

地球の写真の上に衛星のモデルが重ねられている。2024年11月25日に撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic（ロイター） Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ９日 ロイター] - ＮＴＴや三菱電機、三菱ＵＦＪ銀行など５社は９日、多数の低軌道衛星で地球を広くカバーする「メガコンステレーション」の構築・運用とサービス提供で協業を検討すると発表した。通信や観測、測位に加え、データ処理・保管機能を持つ「宇宙データセンター」などの事業化を目指す。

３社のほか、日本政策投資銀行とＮＴＴドコモビジネスが覚書を結んだ。ＮＴＴは光電融合技術を使った次世代通信、三菱電機は衛星開発やシステム全体の設計など、各社が知見を持ち寄りオープンで相互接続を前提とした事業の構築を目指す。

複数の衛星を連携させる衛星コンステレーションは、測位や防災・減災、安全保障などの分野で社会インフラとして活用される機会が増えている。米スペースＸが展開するスターリンクが代表。個々の衛星のカバー範囲は狭いものの、地表に近いため高速で低遅延の通信が期待できる。

FAST

SEOUL, Nov 9 : South Korea's antitrust regulator said on Monday it was imposing a 300.9 billion won ($220.59 million) fine on e-commerce firm Coupang for abusing its dominant position in the food delivery market.
The Korea Fair Trade Commission (FTC) said Coupang required merchants to match favourable terms offered on rival platforms and penalised those that failed to comply, restricting competition in the delivery app sector.
Coupang required restaurants to match six conditions, including menu prices, minimum order amounts, discounts and delivery charges, the FTC said.
Restaurants that failed to comply risked losing a special designation that allowed them to offer discounts and free delivery to Coupang's paid-membership customers, it said.

The regulator said the proportion of restaurants meeting the requirements rose to nearly 94 per cent in October 2025 from about 13 per cent in July 2023.
The FTC also fined Woowa Brothers, the operator of rival delivery app Baemin, 331.1 billion won for similar practices.
Woowa Brothers said in a statement it had explained to the FTC that its conduct was not unlawful and regretted that its arguments had not been fully accepted, adding it would closely review the decision.
Coupang said in a statement the penalty was excessive and more than 600 times the fine imposed in a comparable 2020 case involving another food delivery app.
It said the FTC had included revenue unrelated to the alleged conduct when calculating the fine, undermining its right of defence, and that it would challenge the decision through legal proceedings.
The ruling adds to tensions between US-listed Coupang and South Korean authorities, which fined the company 624 billion won in June over a 2025 data breach affecting more than 33 million customers.
Coupang has disputed the government's findings and handling of that case, while Republican US lawmakers have accused Seoul of discriminating against an American company, a claim South Korean officials reject.
Coupang has maintained an extensive lobbying and political operation in Washington, contributing to figures on both sides of the political aisle.
US Federal Election Commission records show that its political action committee, COUPAC, gave about $379,000 to congressional candidates and political committees from the start of 2025 through September 2026.
Recent records suggest a growing emphasis on cultivating Democratic ties ahead of the party's strong performance in the midterm elections, although COUPAC continued to support Republicans.
($1 = 1,363.6400 won)

[シドニー／ソウル ９日 ロイター] - 米エヌビディアの株価と同社株に連動する無期限先物が、９日の時間外取引で下落した。時価総額で世界最大の半導体メーカーである同社は８日、ジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が外国の情報活動の標的になったかどうかを調査していると明らかにしていた。

取引所ハイパーリキッドで取引される無期限先物と、ブルー・オーシャンのシステムを通じた時間外の株式取引では、価格が１株当たり１８０．３０ドル前後となり、６日のナスダック市場の終値１８６．６４ドルから約３．４％下落した。

ペッパーストーン（メルボルン）のリサーチ担当責任者クリス・ウェストン氏は「データセンターの拡張を巡って多くの憶測が飛び交っている時期に、この事態が株価にとって決してプラスにはならないと、市場は今、示唆しているのだろう」と述べつつ、フアン氏の交代につながるとは考えていないとした。

items.author: CNA
items.summary: The investigation has put a spotlight on Jensen Huang's future given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and his role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.
items.body:

World

Nvidia's out-of-hour shares fall as firm probes CEO Jensen Huang

The investigation has put a spotlight on Jensen Huang's future given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and his role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.

A NVIDIA logo is displayed on a screen at the NVIDIA GTC conference, focused on advances in AI and computing shaping industries, in Berlin, Germany, on Oct 21, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Annegret Hilse)

FAST

Nvidia shares fell in out-of-hours trading on Monday (Nov 9) after an internal investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort put his future at the AI chipmaker under scrutiny.
The internal probe followed a media report that Huang had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who allegedly passed information to Beijing. Huang told Nvidia's employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the relationship.
The investigation, announced on Sunday, has put a spotlight on Huang's future given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and the CEO's role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.
The fallout extended to South Korea, where Madison Huang, Huang's daughter and an Nvidia executive, cancelled a planned visit to Seoul for an Nvidia conference that was set to begin on Monday, according to companies she had been scheduled to meet.

Perpetual futures trading on the Hyperliquid exchange and after-hours shares trading on the Blue Ocean system showed Nvidia prices around US$180.30 a share, down about 3.4 per cent from Friday's Nasdaq closing price of US$186.64.
"The market's probably telling you now this does no favours to the stock whatsoever in a time when there's a lot of conjecture as to the build out of data centres," said Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne.
But Weston said he did not think Huang, whom he described as the "godfather of AI", would be replaced.
"If we genuinely thought he was going to step down ... the stock would be down — it would be an absolute bloodbath, to be honest,” he said.

Source: Reuters/lk

FAST

SYDNEY, Nov 9 : UBS Chief Executive Sergio Ermotti said on Monday a sharp correction in AI stocks over the last few weeks had been a reaction to excessively high hopes that investors had had for the sector.
Speaking at a UBS conference in Sydney, Ermotti said recent US midterm election results and the global debate about the implications of building up infrastructure could lead to delays in the AI sector delivering outcomes.
"And the market until very recently — of course in the last few weeks we saw some correction — has been pricing perfection."
Ermotti said while he was optimistic AI development would generate positive economic outcomes, that he personally believed "the timing on how quickly we will get there, it's a little bit exaggerated."

Trillions of dollars of world stock market value were wiped out last week over fears that Democratic election victories would bring tighter US regulations for the AI industry, though Wall Street equities mostly rallied on Friday.
Ermotti added that some aspects of UBS' own implementation of AI into its operations had been "slowed down" by the integration of Credit Suisse, which it agreed to acquire in a Swiss government-brokered rescue in 2023.
The collapse of Credit Suisse has also left UBS facing the prospect of tougher regulation in Switzerland, and the Zurich-based lender is assessing the long-term consequences of proposed new capital requirements for its ability to compete from its Swiss base.
On Monday, he described the country's response to the situation as "extremely emotional" and "idiosyncratic", contrasting it to authorities in the US and Europe that he said recognised the unintended consequences of over-regulation.

items.title: Iron Ore Falls as China Pollution Curbs Fuel Demand Worries
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Iron ore prices slipped on Monday, weighed down by mounting concerns over demand in top consumer China after steelmakers in key production hubs imposed output curbs to protect air quality. The most-traded iron ore contract on China’s Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE) fell 0.73% to 684.5 …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
Iron ore prices slipped on Monday, weighed down by mounting concerns over demand in top consumer China after steelmakers in key production hubs imposed output curbs to protect air quality.

The most-traded iron ore contract on China’s Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE) fell 0.73% to 684.5 yuan ($102.53) a metric ton by 0145 GMT after hitting a four-week high of 694.5 yuan on November 6.

The benchmark December iron ore on the Singapore Exchange was 0.58% lower at $92.5 a ton, as of 0135 GMT.

Authorities in northern China, including steelmaking hubs Tangshan and Handan in Hebei province, announced emergency response measures from Monday amid forecasts of heavy air pollution, according to official WeChat posts.

Such measures typically require steelmakers to curb production, reducing demand for steelmaking raw materials.

The restrictions added pressure on prices of the key steelmaking ingredient already facing seasonal weakness in demand.

Average daily hot metal output among Chinese steelmakers slid for a fourth straight week, declining 0.5% from the previous week to 2.31 million tons as of November 5, the lowest since late March, consultancy Mysteel data showed.

Hot metal output, a blast furnace product, is widely viewed as a gauge of iron ore demand.

“Iron ore prices will remain under pressure if there is no material improvement in demand at home and abroad in the fourth quarter,” analysts at broker Yongan Futures said in a note.

Coking coal DJMcv1 and coke DCJcv1, other steelmaking ingredients, fell 0.81% and 0.39%, respectively.

Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange were mixed. Rebar SRBcv1 shed 0.16%, hot-rolled coil slid 0.37%, while stainless steel added 0.6%.

items.author: CNA

South Korea says Nvidia issues won't affect contracted GPU supplies

SEOUL: South Korea expects contracted deliveries of Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs) to proceed without disruption despite a controversy surrounding the chipmaker's chief executive Jensen Huang , Seoul's deputy science minister said on Monday (Nov 9).
Vice Minister of Science and ICT Ryu Jemyung told a parliamentary budget committee that 10,000 GPUs funded under a 2025 supplementary budget had already arrived and were in use.
GPUs planned for 2026 were under contract and expected to enter service this year, he said.
"We expect production and the delivery schedule for contracted volumes to proceed without disruption," Ryu said, adding that the ministry was closely monitoring developments and discussing prices and schedules with Nvidia Korea.

Nvidia's board said on Sunday it had opened an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a Chinese intelligence effort through his relationship with businesswoman Alice Huang.

Related:

Nvidia's Huang says dealings with firm in US spy probe were 'normal' as China denies allegations

The board said it had no reason to believe US national security or Nvidia secrets had been compromised, while Huang said he would cooperate fully.
News of the controversy coincided with the cancellation of a visit to South Korea by Huang's daughter Madison Huang, an Nvidia senior director.
South Korean AI startup Rebellions said her planned visit to its headquarters and a partner dinner were cancelled because of unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia.
Kakao Mobility also cancelled a photo session and question-and-answer event with her, but said a business agreement with Nvidia would proceed with senior director Gaurav Agarwal attending instead.
Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day event expected to draw about 2,000 participants to discuss physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure, was proceeding as planned according to South Korean media.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

items.title: US-Israel security pact set to halve direct military aid post-2028 under evolving five-year framework: Report
items.summary: New details reveal US military aid to Israel will not end immediately, but will instead be halved to a five-year package after 2028. Negotiators aim to finalise the memorandum of understanding before ...
items.body:
US-Israel security pact set to halve direct military aid post-2028 under evolving five-year framework: Report  New details reveal US military aid to Israel will not end immediately, but will instead be halved to a five-year package after 2028. Negotiators aim to finalise the memorandum of understanding before January, navigating domestic political hurdles and potential congressional appropriations challenges.
ANI | Updated: 09-11-2026 14:57 IST | Created: 09-11-2026 14:57 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

American military assistance to Israel will not terminate immediately under a forthcoming security memorandum of understanding, with new details uncovered by Ynetnews indicating that direct aid will instead be reduced by roughly half by restricting its duration to a five-year window following 2028 rather than the traditional decade-long span. These revelations surface approximately a week after US President Donald Trump unexpectedly stated that he and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had agreed to halt American military aid by the close of the year, leaving Israeli negotiating teams bewildered by the pronouncement, as reported by Ynetnews.
A senior Israeli official assessed that Trump's declaration was driven primarily by domestic political calculations to assist Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan against Democratic challenger Abdul El-Sayed, though the strategy ultimately proved unsuccessful as El-Sayed secured victory, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate, according to Ynetnews. During a Fox News appearance on Election Day, Trump stated, "We were giving them $4 billion. We are, but it gets cut off at the end of the year." He additionally noted that Netanyahu had previously raised the concept of phasing out assistance on the grounds that Israel had evolved into a prosperous nation no longer requiring such backing.
Nevertheless, the evolving framework does not contemplate an immediate stoppage, with current assistance remaining fully active through 2028 under the prevailing model that grants USD 3.3 billion yearly in Foreign Military Financing alongside USD 500 million for joint defence research, Ynetnews noted. Under the revised terms under discussion by teams representing US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Israel's Defence Ministry, annual funding levels would remain comparable for a shortened five-year period totalling roughly USD 16.5 billion before direct military provisions cease.
Meanwhile, American allocations dedicated to collaborative air and missile defence advancement are anticipated to climb from the present USD 500 million annually to an amount yet to be finalised. Furthermore, a senior Israeli official familiar with the diplomatic exchanges observed that numerous members of Congress resist lowering assistance due to domestic economic factors, given that the vast majority of funds flow directly back into American manufacturing plants and local state economies, as detailed by Ynetnews.
"We are moving here from a model of aid to a model of partnership," the senior Israeli official stated, adding, "It is important to remember that most of the security assistance remains in America and contributes to the American economy. Cutting it would also hurt American industries and require adjustments." While negotiators aim to conclude the pact prior to the new Congress convening in January, Israeli planners remain wary regarding annual congressional appropriation hurdles and potential political friction.
Officials have acknowledged that future government compositions and leadership figures will heavily influence legislative backing in Washington, Ynetnews reported. (ANI)

items.title: Nvidia's shares slide as chip giant probes CEO Huang over spy claims
items.summary: Nvidia's shares tumbled more than 6% in Frankfurt trading, extending last week's selloff and pushing the stock to fresh multi-month lows ...
items.body:
Home / Markets / News / Nvidia's shares slide as chip giant probes CEO Huang over spy claims

Nvidia's shares slide as chip giant probes CEO Huang over spy claims Nvidia's shares tumbled more than 6% in Frankfurt trading, extending last week's selloff and pushing the stock to fresh multi-month lows

Nvidia shares fell sharply on Monday. (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters 5 min read Last Updated : Nov 09 2026 | 2:42 PM IST

Nvidia shares fell sharply on Monday after an internal investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort put his future at the AI chipmaker under scrutiny.  
The internal probe ??followed a media report that Huang had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who allegedly passed information to Beijing. Huang told Nvidia's employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the relationship.  
The investigation, announced on Sunday, has put a spotlight on Huang's future given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and the CEO's role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.  
 

The leather-jacketed Huang enjoys rock-star status worldwide, particularly in Asia, where he often mingles freely with fans, taking selfies and signing autographs for his devoted followers.  
The fallout from the probe extended to South Korea, where Madison Huang, Huang's daughter and an Nvidia executive, cancelled a planned visit to Seoul for an Nvidia conference that was set to begin on Monday, according to companies she had been scheduled to meet.  
Also Read

Nvidia CEO Huang probe: China calls 'spy narrative' unsubstantiated

Chinese newspaper dismisses Nvidia CEO Huang spy claim, warns on ties

Jensen Huang is bigger than Nvidia, and that spells trouble for AI

From Trump to Bill Ackman: Reactions to Nvidia's probe into CEO Huang

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair admission counters past statements on ties

Nvidia's shares tumbled more than 6% in Frankfurt trading, extending last week's selloff and pushing the stock to fresh multi-month lows. At those levels, the chipmaker stood to lose about $270 billion from its closing price on Friday, according to LSEG Datastream.  

"The market's probably telling you now this does no favours to the stock whatsoever in a time when there's a lot of conjecture as to the build-out of data centres," said Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne.
But Weston said he did not think Huang, whom he described as the "godfather of AI", would be replaced.
"If we genuinely thought he was going to step down ... the stock would be down - it would be an absolute bloodbath, to be honest," he said.  
The New York Times reported last month that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

"The so-called Chinese spy narrative is purely a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters in Beijing.  
Megaspeed did not respond immediately to a request for comment on Monday, a public holiday in Singapore.
Alice Huang did not respond to the New York Times last month when it first reported her relationship with Huang, and Reuters could not determine her location to seek comment on Monday.
  ASIA PARTNERS UNAFFECTED  
Shares in Nvidia's key Asian chip suppliers TSMC, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix rebounded on Monday after last week's selloff of AI-related stocks. TSMC shares jumped 6.5%, while those in Samsung and SK Hynix climbed 2.9% and 4.7%, respectively.  

Some prominent figures weighed in on Huang's admission. Billionaire investor Bill Ackman, founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, said on X that the Nvidia CEO was an "incredible human," but if "indeed this is more than an affair, then it is obviously a real problem."  
"I am hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security," he added.  
Tesla CEO Elon Musk commented, "I agree", on a post by Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire that said Huang "did something incredibly dumb" that was "bad ??for America" but that "Jensen is irreplaceable for America's AI leadership".
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he had not spoken to Huang about the allegations, but called him a fine person. "I hope everything's fine. He's done such an incredible job," he added.  

When asked if he believed he should have acted on intelligence when he was briefed about it, Trump said: "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it."
The New York Times reported that Trump was briefed about the intelligence findings roughly a year ago and chose not to do anything with the information.
  CANCELLED VISIT  
Madison Huang had initially planned to visit South Korean AI startup Rebellions and hold a question-and-answer session with Kakao Mobility. Rebellions said the events were cancelled due to "unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia."

Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day event expected to draw about 2,000 participants to discuss physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure, will proceed as planned, according to South Korean media. Nvidia did not respond immediately to a request for comment.  
Analysts said a prolonged investigation or internal review could potentially delay Nvidia's investment decisions or product launches, with broader implications for the semiconductor industry.  
Ryu Young-ho, a senior analyst at NH Investment & Securities, said Nvidia's rivals, including Advanced Micro Devices, could attract greater attention in the short term, potentially putting Samsung, which has close business ties with AMD, in the spotlight.

Still, he said Nvidia's products would be difficult to replace, limiting the potential impact, although shipments to China could face further delays depending on how the situation developed.  
South Korea's deputy science minister said on Monday the government expected no disruptions to contracted deliveries of Nvidia graphics processing units despite issues currently facing the company.   (Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

items.title: Bill Gates says billionaires should pay more taxes as AI reshapes economy
items.summary: Gates said that governments must take primary responsibility for tackling inequality as AI generates wealth, warning that philanthropy cannot replace public support systems ...
items.body:
Home / Technology / Tech News / Bill Gates says billionaires should pay more taxes as AI reshapes economy

Bill Gates says billionaires should pay more taxes as AI reshapes economy Gates said that governments must take primary responsibility for tackling inequality as AI generates wealth, warning that philanthropy cannot replace public support systems

Gates also highlighted the need to reconsider how governments tax labour and capital as businesses increasingly adopt AI tools and automation | Image: Bloomberg

Apexa Rai New Delhi 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 09 2026 | 1:49 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates has called for governments to reconsider taxation policies and ensure that billionaires and wealthy individuals contribute more towards addressing inequality, as the rapid growth of artificial intelligence(AI) threatens to widen the gap between rich and poor.
  Speaking on the Financial Times' Tech Tonic podcast, Gates said governments must take primary responsibility for tackling economic inequality, rather than relying on charitable contributions from wealthy individuals.
  "The primary responsibility of dealing with inequality will always rest with governments. We can't expect philanthropy, which is voluntary in nature, to be the safety net," Gates said.
  He argued that tax systems would need to adapt to an economy increasingly shaped by AI , including ensuring that people with substantial wealth and billionaires contribute towards public welfare.
 

  The comments come amid growing concerns that the economic gains from AI could remain concentrated among technology companies, investors and wealthy individuals, even as automation changes the nature of employment across industries.
Also Read

  Gates also highlighted the need to reconsider how governments tax labour and capital as businesses increasingly adopt AI tools and automation. Existing tax structures, he said, can make investment in machines more financially attractive than employing people.
  In an essay published on his website, Gates Notes, he had previously proposed taxing robots, arguing that automation could otherwise accelerate job displacement without generating equivalent contributions towards public finances.
  The Microsoft co-founder believes governments could use tax revenues to support workers affected by technological changes.

  Gates, who has pledged to give away virtually all his wealth through the Gates Foundation over the next two decades, maintains that charitable giving cannot substitute for government-funded welfare and public services.

items.author: CNA
items.summary: Both the US and Iran have continued strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, however, restricting exports of energy and other commodities vital to the world economy.
items.body:

Trump says he is highly unlikely to order Iran strikes if talks progress

Both the US and Iran have continued strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, however, restricting exports of energy and other commodities vital to the world economy.

People protest against military action in Iran near the White House in Washington DC, on Apr 8, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Evelyn Hockstein)

WASHINGTON/CAIRO: US President Donald Trump on Sunday (Nov 8) said he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progress , even as both countries reported that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz.
"It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."
CNN did not specify exactly what it had asked Trump, who also said that if strikes resume, the US has identified potential infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges "that we can knock down in literally one hour".
Trump had hinted at renewing major attacks on Iran after last week's US midterm elections, but there has been no sign of a large-scale US military operation. Iran has said it would respond by striking US and Israeli targets.

Iran ian media suggested that explosions in southern Iran on Saturday were related to Iran ian military activities rather than US strikes.
Iran 's state television said officials had not confirmed any missile strikes on Iran ian territory following blasts heard in several areas, including on Qeshm Island in the strait.
Both the US and Iran have continued strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, however, restricting exports of energy and other commodities vital to the world economy.
Iran 's state television said the evening explosions might be related to Iran ian military activity in the waterway, where Iran said two vessels had hit mines and a third had caught fire.

Related:

US launches task force to disrupt land transit routes into Iran

Iran says forces 'stronger' than at beginning of war

The US said its air force had disabled a vessel in the Gulf of Oman beyond the strait.
Tasnim news agency said two missiles had struck Qeshm Island, with no official information on possible damage. Neither Iran nor the US has commented on that report. Washington said on Nov 2 that it had struck the island in a limited defensive measure against Iran ians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets.
COMMERCIAL VESSEL, OIL TANKERS HIT Since the US and Israel began attacks on Iran in February, Tehran has sought the upper hand by hitting vessels in the Strait of Hormuz to block Gulf energy exports, while US forces began blockading movements to and from Iran ian ports in April.
The US military said on Saturday evening that its air force had fired at the stern of a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman, disabling it as it tried to get through the blockade.
Iran 's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two oil tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to pass through an "unauthorised route" in the Strait of Hormuz. A third tanker had also suffered an explosion and caught fire, the semi-official Fars news agency reported later.
Reuters was not able to confirm any of the reported strikes.
Monitors from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said a bulk carrier and military forces were involved in an incident in the Gulf of Oman, approximately 18 nautical miles east of the United Arab Emirates' city of Khor Fakkan, with damage unknown. It was unclear if it was related to the reported US attack.

Smoke rises from the stern of a St. Kitts-flagged cargo vessel following what US Central Command says was a strike on Saturday to disable the vessel, which was trying to break the US blockade of Iran, at a location given as the Gulf of Oman, in this still image taken from video released Nov 7, 2026. (Photo: Handout via REUTERS/US Central Command)

SAUDI STATE OIL COMPANY BUILDING DAMAGED A conflict between Iran -aligned Houthis in Yemen and Saudi Arabia has escalated this month, enlarging the wider Middle East war.
On Sunday, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said an administrative building belonging to state oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh had been damaged by falling debris after an attempted attack, with no injuries or fatalities reported.
Qatar, which has been mediating in talks to try to end the conflict that has shaken the world economy, on Saturday denied reports that the US and Iran had failed to reach a deal.
The Qatari prime minister had affirmed that both sides were continuing to work toward an agreement, it said.
Iran has submitted a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar, a senior Iran ian official told Reuters on Thursday, saying the US was reviewing it but discussions would depend on Washington first meeting Tehran's seven demands.
These include sanctions relief, access to frozen assets and war reparations, while Washington insists nuclear issues must feature in initial talks.
On Saturday, the US military said it was launching a task force to crack down on the movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material to Iran via its land borders and the Caspian Sea — part of economic measures to try to pressure Tehran.
Iran 's Revolutionary Guards dismissed the plan as "wordplay", saying it would not work because Tehran had made preparations and communicated closely with its neighbours.

Source: Reuters/fs

items.title: Brazil picks 27 critical minerals in push for local supply chain
items.author: Mining.com
items.creator: Mining.com
items.summary: Brazil has designated 27 critical minerals as the country looks to accelerate mineral projects, develop the sector domestically and reduce its reliance on e
items.body: Brazil has designated 27 critical minerals as the country looks to accelerate mineral projects, develop the sector domestically and reduce its reliance on exporting raw materials. The National Council for Industrialization of Critical and Strategic Minerals (CIMCE) approved the list on Nov. 5, dividing the minerals into three priority groups based on their importance to national security, industrial development and supply chain resilience. The classification will help determine which mining projects qualify for federal support. “For so long we have exported mineral wealth as ore and imported it back as a finished product, developing value and jobs in other countries,” development, industry, commerce and services minister, Brazil’s minister of development, industry, commerce and services, Márcio Elias Rosa, said. “We want to stop this cycle and create a strategy to develop this here.” The initiative comes as countries seek to diversify supplies of minerals essential to electric vehicles, renewable energy, defence and advanced technologies. Brazil hopes to capture more value from its mineral resources by encouraging investment in refining and manufacturing rather than relying primarily on raw material exports. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said the government intends to work with international partners rather than control the industry outright. “We don’t want the state to have absolute control over exploration, processing and industrialization,” Lula said during the council meeting, according to Bloomberg. “We need to work with other countries that want to join us in developing and processing this wealth.” Only the 27 minerals included in the list, and nationally registered projects, will be eligible to receive government support, according to the new government strategy. The list The council identified nine high-priority minerals: rare earths, graphite, lithium, nickel, cobalt, copper, manganese, silicon and uranium. The government said high-priority minerals have a high geopolitical risk, global demand and low substitution rate for other materials, CNN Brasil reported. “The list will function as the compass of Brazilian mineral politics, giving the sector the most important tool: predictability,” the mines and energy ministry said in a statement to G1. Eight minerals fall into the medium-priority category: tungsten, chrome, vanadium, tantalum, titanium, phosphate, potassium and sulfur. The remaining 10 are classified as lower priority: niobium, tin, iron, zinc, gold, magnesium, molybdenum, thorium, aluminum and platinum group metals. The classifications will undergo reviews every four years to account for economic, technological and geopolitical developments. Investment priority Having this list will allow the government to direct financing toward projects that strengthen domestic mineral production and processing. The rules for approval or denial of projects still need to be defined. The council also created a fund to reduce risks and expand investments in the sector, known as FGAM. It can receive up to R$2 billion (about $364 million) from the federal government as well as more from local and state governments and private investment. A separate Federal Program for Critical and Strategic Minerals (PFMCE) will have an annual funding limit of R$1 billion ($180 million) between 2030 and 2034 so companies can invest in mining development and transformation. The measures follow Lula’s approval in September of R$5 billion (about $909 million) in funding to advance rare earths exploration, part of Brazil’s broader push to develop its mineral industry. Both the council and government aim to have another meeting on this issue before the end of the year to better define supply chain priorities to advance investment decisions in the sector. The list will be reassessed every four years and may undergo changes based on economical, technological or geopolitical changes across the globe. (With files from Bloomberg)

Marina Meireles | November 8, 2026 | 11:37 am

Caldeira rare earth project location. ( Image courtesy of Meteoric Resources | Facebook. )

Brazil has designated 27 critical minerals as the country looks to accelerate mineral projects, develop the sector domestically and reduce its reliance on exporting raw materials. 

The National Council for Industrialization of Critical and Strategic Minerals (CIMCE) approved the list on Nov. 5, dividing the minerals into three priority groups based on their importance to national security, industrial development and supply chain resilience. The classification will help determine which mining projects qualify for federal support. 

“For so long we have exported mineral wealth as ore and imported it back as a finished product, developing value and jobs in other countries,” development, industry, commerce and services minister, Brazil’s minister of development, industry, commerce and services, Márcio Elias Rosa, said. “We want to stop this cycle and create a strategy to develop this here.” 

The initiative comes as countries seek to diversify supplies of minerals essential to electric vehicles, renewable energy, defence and advanced technologies.  

Brazil hopes to capture more value from its mineral resources by encouraging investment in refining and manufacturing rather than relying primarily on raw material exports. 

President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said the government intends to work with international partners rather than control the industry outright. 

“We don’t want the state to have absolute control over exploration, processing and industrialization,” Lula said during the council meeting, according to Bloomberg. “We need to work with other countries that want to join us in developing and processing this wealth.” 

Only the 27 minerals included in the list, and nationally registered projects, will be eligible to receive government support, according to the new government strategy.  

The list  

The council identified nine high-priority minerals: rare earths, graphite, lithium, nickel, cobalt, copper, manganese, silicon and uranium. The government said high-priority minerals have a high geopolitical risk, global demand and low substitution rate for other materials, CNN Brasil reported . 

“The list will function as the compass of Brazilian mineral politics, giving the sector the most important tool: predictability,” the mines and energy ministry said in a statement to G1 .  

Eight minerals fall into the medium-priority category: tungsten, chrome, vanadium, tantalum, titanium, phosphate, potassium and sulfur. The remaining 10 are classified as lower priority: niobium, tin, iron, zinc, gold, magnesium, molybdenum, thorium, aluminum and platinum group metals.  

The classifications will undergo reviews every four years to account for economic, technological and geopolitical developments. 

Investment priority  

Having this list will allow the government to direct financing toward projects that strengthen domestic mineral production and processing. The rules for approval or denial of projects still need to be defined.  

The council also created a fund to reduce risks and expand investments in the sector, known as FGAM. It can receive up to R$2 billion (about $364 million) from the federal government as well as more from local and state governments and private investment.  

A separate Federal Program for Critical and Strategic Minerals (PFMCE) will have an annual funding limit of R$1 billion ($180 million) between 2030 and 2034 so companies can invest in mining development and transformation.  

The measures follow Lula’s approval in September of R$5 billion (about $909 million) in funding to advance rare earths exploration, part of Brazil’s broader push to develop its mineral industry.

Both the council and government aim to have another meeting on this issue before the end of the year to better define supply chain priorities to advance investment decisions in the sector.  

The list will be reassessed every four years and may undergo changes based on economical, technological or geopolitical changes across the globe.

items.title: Nasdaq dives 5.6% after Democrats’ win, VIX rises 70% on AI and Fed fears
items.author: Cointurk
items.creator: Cointurk
items.summary: Wall Street is preparing for a volatile start to Monday, November 9, following a sharp technology-led selloff, renewed US military actions in Iran, and heig
items.body: Wall Street is preparing for a volatile start to Monday, November 9, following a sharp technology-led selloff, renewed US military actions in Iran, and heightened speculation about another Federal Reserve rate hike. Despite warnings from some market observers about a potential “Black Monday” crash, evidence of an imminent collapse remains limited. Tech stocks tumble after Democrats take Congress Volatility spikes as VIX soars but crash remains unconfirmed Geopolitical pressure and Fed expectations fuel uncertainty Tech stocks tumble after Democrats take Congress The Nasdaq Composite plummeted 5.56% on November 5, as investors reevaluated technology sector prospects after the Democratic Party secured control of Congress in the US midterm elections. This shift has fueled concerns over stricter regulations related to artificial intelligence and increased operational costs for data centers, raising doubts about the pace of future infrastructure development. Reuters reported that the S&P 500 declined about 4.4% the same day, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average shed more than 1,800 points. The initial optimism following Wednesday’s market rally quickly vanished, replaced by fears that legislative changes could limit growth in AI and related industries. In the credit markets, traders sought higher yields for corporate bonds issued by AI-focused companies. While this trend highlights tighter lending conditions, it does not necessarily point to widespread capital flight from the sector. Mini dictionary: S&P 500 is a major US stock market index composed of 500 leading publicly traded companies, often considered a primary benchmark for the overall US equity market. The sharp Nasdaq drop reflected growing unease over government oversight and rising costs in the artificial intelligence sector following Democratic gains in Congress. Index Change (%) Result Nasdaq Composite -5.56% Major decline S&P 500 -4.4% Significant drop Dow Jones -1,800 pts Steep fall Volatility spikes as VIX soars but crash remains unconfirmed The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX), often called Wall Street’s “fear gauge,” jumped nearly 70% on November 5, climbing from 16.61 to 28.18. This move marked the third-largest single-day percentage increase since 1990, though the VIX stayed below crisis-era extremes. By Friday, the VIX moderated to 25.64 as semiconductor stocks contributed to a partial rebound. The Nasdaq recovered 1.1% and the S&P 500 edged up 0.3%, but both benchmarks ended the week with overall losses, reflecting lingering market anxiety. Analysts cautioned that the late recovery did not eliminate the risk of renewed selling. Friday’s recovery provided some relief after Thursday’s steep losses, yet continuing volatility left investors wary ahead of Monday’s trading session. Geopolitical pressure and Fed expectations fuel uncertainty Tensions increased after US President Donald Trump confirmed targeted strikes against Iranian air defense installations on Qeshm Island. This action followed previous US military operations amid the ongoing conflict with Iran. Rising concerns over the security of the Strait of Hormuz continued to affect global risk sentiment and oil markets. The US labor market report released on Friday showed that American employers added 165,000 jobs in October, well above expectations of 65,000. Unemployment fell to 4.1%. Futures pricing suggested a 78% chance that the Federal Reserve would raise rates in December, intensifying pressure on technology companies that rely on low-cost financing. Higher borrowing expenses threaten to squeeze profits for heavily leveraged tech firms and data center operators. The outlook for Monday’s market open remains highly uncertain, as investors grapple with unresolved geopolitical tensions and ongoing economic policy debates. While risks have risen, current data do not confirm a repeat of previous “Black Monday” style crashes. items.title: Ontario’s Lecce warns that Democrats offer no tariff cure
items.author: Northern Miner Staff
items.creator: Northern Miner Staff
items.summary: Canada shouldn’t expect the United States to lift tariffs simply because Democrats won control of Congress, Ontario Energy and Mines Minister said.
items.body:
Ontario’s Lecce warns that Democrats offer no tariff cure

Frédéric Tomesco | November 5, 2026 | 4:00 pm
Regulatory Issues   Canada   USA   Aluminum   Copper   Nickel  

Ontario Energy and Mines Minister Stephen Lecce (in a file photo) says Canada still faces U.S. protectionism regardless of the midterm elections. Credit: The Northern Miner

Canada shouldn’t expect the United States to lift tariffs simply because Democrats won control of Congress , Ontario Energy and Mines Minister Stephen Lecce said.

Speaking two days after the U.S. midterm elections, Lecce said the outcome could strengthen Prime Minister Mark Carney’s negotiating position. Still, protectionism runs through both major U.S. political parties, which will leave Canadian exporters exposed even after President Donald Trump leaves office, he cautioned.

“I’m just not convinced it materially changes our fundamental reality on the ground,” Lecce said of the U.S. midterm election results in a lunchtime speech Thursday to the Empire Club of Toronto. “The change of the composition of Congress doesn’t change the policy position of America vis-a-vis tariffs.”

Lecce’s remarks underscore the gap between securing a trade agreement and eliminating tariffs. For Canadian metals producers, a trade deal may offer greater certainty without removing the tariffs that raise the cost of selling into the U.S. market.

Lame-duck Trump

Democrats won both the House of Representatives and Senate in Tuesday’s elections, giving them power to challenge Trump’s agenda when the new Congress convenes in January. The results leave the Republican president facing an opposition-controlled Congress for his final two years in office.

While U.S. political analysts pointed to voter frustration over high prices, the Iran war and government corruption as key factors behind Tuesday’s outcome, Lecce insists trade friction with Canada figured prominently in the campaign.

“Tariffs were on the ballot,” he said. “We stayed in our lane, but it’s clear that Canada was on the ballot.”

New momentum

Negotiations between the neighbours and trading partners have been showing fresh momentum. Carney said Tuesday that Washington had dropped demands affecting Canada’s ability to negotiate agreements with other countries. Trump, meanwhile, said a deal was close, Reuters reported.

Carney’s recent comments on the state of talks are “a good signal,” Lecce said. The Democrats’ win Tuesday “perhaps will enable a better hand for Prime Minister Carney and the national government to land a deal.”

Ontario Premier Doug Ford should get credit for pressing Carney to reject an earlier agreement that would have entrenched tariffs, Lecce added.

Recounting a conversation between the two leaders, Lecce said Ford told Carney this summer: “’Do not sign a bad deal that will lock us and create the precedent of acceptance of tariffs in perpetuity. No deal is materially better than a good deal.”

Ford also made it clear to Carney that Ontario would oppose the deal publicly, according to Lecce.

Wider dispute

Ottawa suspended negotiations with the U.S. in August. Washington subsequently imposed 50% tariffs on $27.6 billion of Canadian goods, prompting Canadian countermeasures .

The dispute extends beyond those measures. According to Canada’s Trade Commissioner Service, U.S. sectoral tariffs on covered steel, aluminum and copper products range from 15% to 50%, subject to product and content rules. Certain other tariffs apply even when Canadian goods qualify for preferential treatment under the continental trade agreement.

The bilateral talks are unfolding alongside negotiations over the Canada–United States–Mexico Agreement, or CUSMA. The pact replaced the North American Free Trade Agreement in July 2020, following renegotiation during Trump’s first presidency.

Washington declined to extend CUSMA in its current form at the July 1 review. That triggered annual reviews rather than immediate expiry: the agreement’s existing term runs to 2036, and the three countries can jointly approve another 16-year term.

Canada has explicitly linked those discussions to relief from sectoral tariffs on steel, aluminum, autos and lumber. Preserving CUSMA and resolving the tariff dispute therefore remain connected negotiating objectives.

Diversification

Even as efforts advance to rebuild the American relationship, Canada and Ontario should continue to deepen ties with other nations, Lecce argued.

“We should strengthen that relationship [with the U.S.], get it back on track, but be very vigorous in diversification,” he said. Ontario’s goal is “to make sure we are less exposed, less shocked by that vulnerability when conservatively, well over 75% of our trade is going to one nation.”

Even so, “it doesn’t mean that we can’t hope for some return to what I’d call just normal, respectful civil dialog with the most foundational relationship on earth, which is the United States.”

items.title: AngloGold plans $900 million mine expansion amid stronger profit
items.author: Marina Meireles
items.creator: Marina Meireles
items.summary: The investment comes as the gold miner aims to incrementally increase production by the end of the decade.
items.body:
AngloGold plans $900 million mine expansion amid stronger profit 

Marina Meireles | November 5, 2026 | 9:55 am
Top Companies   Africa   Latin America   Gold  

Geita open pit mine, located in northwestern Tanzania, is AngloGold’s largest single gold mining operation. ( Image: AngloGold Ashanti )

AngloGold Ashanti (NYSE: AU) plans to invest up to $900 million in expanding brownfield operations across its portfolio, targeting a production increase of 300,000 ounces to 450,000 ounces by 2030. 

The investments will focus on the Geita gold mine in Tanzania, Siguiri in Guinea and Cuiabá in Brazil, as well as the ongoing ramp-up at Obuasi in Ghana. The company expects the projects to generate real internal rates of return exceeding 35%, Reuters reported. 

“These are high-return, capital efficient projects at our operating mines that are expected to provide high-margin ounces and unlock further value from our portfolio,” AngloGold Ashanti CEO Alberto Calderon said in a statement. 

The plan is to use existing infrastructure and operational footprints to reduce risk and optimize capital intensity. 

Geita will receive the larger portion of the funding, up to $580 million to raise output to 600,000 ounces by 2030. Cuiabá’s expansion will cost between $200 million and $250 million, adding about 75,000 ounces to its output. 

Another $70 million will be put towards the Suguiri mine, looking to add another 100,000 ounces to its production. 

Shares in AngloGold Ashanti were up 0.35% to $88.22 apiece by mid-day Thursday in New York, valuing the company at $44.6 billion. 

Profit on the rise  

AngloGold reported a 12% increase for its EBITDA for Q3 2026 to $1,568 million, from $1,400 million for Q3 2025.  

The company said on its Q3 earnings release that the growth is supported by the increase in the average gold price received per ounce to $4,239/oz, from $3,490/oz in the same period in 2025. 

AngloGold Ashanti said its full year gold production guidance of 2,800,000 ounces to 3,170,000 ounces is reaffirmed.  

Its gold production was about 3.65% more costly than the previous quarter, at $1,534 per ounce due gold royalties and higher fuel costs.  

The company also reported that a worker died due to a rockfall at the Sukari underground mine in August 2026. Operations were suspended while investigations took place, but have since resumed. 

(With files from Reuters)

The Company has sold from treasury a total of 288,150 Ordinary shares of 1p each in the capital of the Company today at an average price of 260.7785 pence per share. These shares will rank pari passu with the existing ordinary shares in issue.
Following this transaction, the Company hereby notifies the market that the resultant number of Ordinary shares held by the Company in treasury is 20,274,901 and the total number of Ordinary shares that the Company has in issue, including shares held in treasury, is 114,920,697. The total number of voting rights in the Company following the re-issue is 94,645,796.
The figure of 94,645,796 may be used by shareholders as the denominator for the calculation by which they may determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or change to their interest in, the Company under the FCA's Disclosure and Transparency Rules.

items.title: テンセントがオラクルからAI半導体10万個をリース、70億ドル規模－FT
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国のテンセント・ホールディングス（騰訊）は、東南アジアでオラクルから先端のAI半導体を借り受けることで合意した。テンセントにとってAI半導体のリース契約としては過去最大規模となる。英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（FT）が事情に詳しい関係者の話として報じた。

報道によると、テンセントは、5年間の契約の一環として10万個の半導体を利用できるようになる。契約額は70億ドル（約1兆1000億円）に上るという。

中国のAI開発企業は米国の輸出規制を回避するため、米エヌビディア製など中国国内では入手できないAIアクセラレーターを海外で借りて利用している。中国のテクノロジー企業は、東南アジアのデータセンターの最大顧客層の一つとなっている。

テンセントとオラクルの担当者は、ブルームバーグ・ニュースのコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。

原題：Tencent Leases AI Chips From Oracle
